parts.content:
Audit this repository's knowledge bundle, .okf/, against its code: every
concept in it (the manifesto, decisions, architecture pages, practices and
any other section), but not handoffs or the log.

For each concept:

1. Read the whole concept, including any Correction sections, which amend
   it; a decision that is deprecated or superseded only claims that its
   successor exists and links back.
2. List its concrete claims about the code: files and folders that exist,
   what a command or function does, defaults, the steps a workflow runs,
   which test enforces an invariant, how parts connect. Correction sections
   make claims too. Every option name, default, number and limit a concept
   states is a claim of its own: search for the option or value and read
   the line that sets it, rather than judging the concept as a whole.
3. Check each claim against the code: find it with search_files or
   list_files, then read the lines that decide it. Skills may help: read a
   matching review skill's SKILL.md before you start, but do the checking
   yourself.
4. Put the concept in checked, saying what you compared it against. Make a
   finding for each claim the code contradicts: the claim is the concept's
   line, contradicted_by the code's lines, and the fix says what the
   concept should say (a decision gets a Correction section, never an edit
   to its body).

Judge only what a concept claims. A claim you could not find the code for
is a medium finding that says what you searched for. Every concept gets a
checked entry, and the summary says how many concepts and claims you
checked.

## Skills

A skill is a folder of instructions for one kind of task. When a skill
matches your task, or part of it, read its SKILL.md with read_file before
you start and follow it. Paths a skill names are relative to its own folder.

- architecture-review: Review instructions for .okf/architecture/ pages, used through /audit and its kmctl-auditor agent - does each design page and diagram still match the code it describes? Use through /audit; read directly when someone asks how architecture pages are judged.
  (/home/vscode/kmctl.worktrees/audit-prompts/apm/.apm/skills/architecture-review/SKILL.md)
- audit: Audit a repository's .okf/ knowledge for drift - architecture pages that no longer match the code, decisions a later decision or the code has overtaken, practices whose evidence is gone - and report findings without changing anything. Use when someone asks to audit, review or check the knowledge bundle, the decision log, the architecture docs or the practices, asks "is our documentation still true", or runs /audit, optionally naming one kind ("audit the architecture docs").

- decision-log-review: Review instructions for .okf/decisions/ records, used through /audit and its kmctl-auditor agent - does each decision still hold, or has a later decision or the code overtaken it? Use through /audit; read directly when someone asks how decision records are judged.

- handoff: Write a technical handoff of the current work to .okf/handoffs/ so you, or another agent, can pick it up later with /continue. Use at the end of a work session, when wrapping up a long conversation, or whenever the user says "hand this off", "write up where we are", "save this so I can continue later", "I'll come back to this", or runs /handoff.
  (/home/vscode/kmctl.worktrees/audit-prompts/apm/.apm/skills/handoff/SKILL.md)
- practices-review: Review instructions for .okf/practices/ pages, used through /audit and its kmctl-auditor agent - does each practice still have the count or code site it cites as evidence? Use through /audit; read directly when someone asks how practices are judged.

- write-docs: Write one page in a repository's docs/ for the people who use the project, filed by Diataxis type (tutorial, how-to, reference or explanation). Use this whenever someone asks to document a feature, write a guide, a getting-started walkthrough, a how-to, a CLI or config reference, or a page explaining why something works the way it does, in a repository with a docs/ folder or a kmctl set-up. Not for decisions, design notes, spikes or handoffs; those go in .okf/.
  (/home/vscode/kmctl.worktrees/audit-prompts/apm/.apm/skills/write-docs/SKILL.md)

## Your report

Finish with a report: a short summary, a checked list and a findings list.

- checked: one entry per page, concept or file you compared, naming what you
  compared it against, with evidence. Something that holds goes here, never
  in findings.
- findings: mismatches only. Each names the claim that does not hold
  (path:line), the lines that contradict it (path:line), and a suggested
  fix. Give each a severity: high for something wrong that someone must
  fix, medium for something that is probably wrong or that you could not
  check, low for something minor, info for a note that needs no fix.

Cite a line as path:line, or a range as path:first-last, with the path
relative to the repository. The report is checked: a citation of a line you
did not read with read_file or get as a search_files hit, or of a line past
the file's end, is sent back.

6|# /audit: check knowledge against reality, report only
7|
8|The audit reads; it never edits `.okf/` or `docs/`, and it writes no
9|`verified` entry (ADR 0005). The person reading the report decides what to fix.

11|## 1. Get what is due
12|
13|```
14|kmctl review due --json
15|```
16|
17|Keep the entries in `due` whose id starts with `architecture/`, `decisions/` or
18|`practices/`. Other kinds (the manifesto, proposals, prototypes, handoffs) are
19|not audited here; mention how many you left out. An id starting with `docs/`
20|is a user page in `docs/`, due because its `stale_after` passed or one of its
21|`sources` changed; list those separately as pages for a person to check, and
22|do not audit them. Never run `kmctl check --fix` or anything else that writes:
23|it regenerates `docs/` folder indexes, and the audit changes nothing. If the user named one kind,
24|keep only that kind. If the user named concepts, use those whether or not
25|they are due. If nothing is left, say nothing in scope is due and stop.
26|
27|## 2. Batch by kind
28|
29|Group the concepts by kind and split each group into batches of at most ten,
30|so each run reads a manageable amount.
31|
32|## 3. Hand each batch to the auditor
33|
34|Read the review skill for the batch's kind, next to this skill in the plugin:
35|`../architecture-review/SKILL.md`, `../decision-log-review/SKILL.md` or
36|`../practices-review/SKILL.md`. Dispatch the `kmctl-auditor` agent with the
37|repository root, the batch (id, path and reasons from step 1) and that review
38|skill's text. The agent has only Read, Grep and Glob, so it cannot change
39|anything. Run batches in parallel when there are several.
40|
41|## 4. Report
42|
43|Collect the agents' JSON blocks. Show a table per kind with each concept, its
44|verdict and its one-line summary, `drifted` first, then `unsure`, then
45|`holds`, followed by the evidence for anything drifted. End with the counts and
46|the combined JSON block, so a script or the CI action can read it. Do not fix
47|anything or offer edits unless the user asks.

12|# Manifesto: kmctl
13|
14|A repository's knowledge is only useful while it is true, and nothing can
15|force it to stay true. An agent can forget to update a decision, and no
16|deterministic hook can tell whether an architecture page still matches the
17|code. kmctl does not pretend otherwise. It does two things instead:
18|
19|1. **It puts the right knowledge in front of the agent** at the start of
20|   every session: where knowledge lives, the rules for writing it, and what
21|   is due for review. Injecting into context works in every harness; a page
22|   the agent has to find does not (ADR 0002).
23|2. **It audits.** A separate agent checks, on request or in CI, that
24|   decisions still hold, the architecture still matches the code and the
25|   practices still have their evidence. It reports; a person decides
26|   (ADR 0005).
27|
28|kmctl came out of the setup in `loop-harness` v2, which worked and which
29|this formalizes so every repository can have it.
30|
31|## Where knowledge lives
32|
33|| Kind | Where | Reader |
34||---|---|---|
35|| Docs for people who use the project | `docs/`, sorted by Diataxis: `tutorials/`, `how-to/`, `reference/`, `explanation/` | users |
36|| Durable project knowledge | `.okf/`, an OKF v0.2 bundle | agents and people working on the project |
37|| Repeatable tasks | skills | agents |
38|| General maxims and strategies | rules | agents |
39|
40|`.okf/` has these sections, each created with its first page: `manifesto.md`
41|(the root concept), `decisions/`, `architecture/`, `practices/`,
42|`proposals/`, `prototypes/` and `handoffs/`. A repository may add its own.
43|
44|## Parts
45|
46|- **`kmctl`, a standalone CLI** (ADR 0001). It serves the briefing that is
47|  injected into context, installs its package and checks the install
48|  (`kmctl doctor`, which writes nothing), and does the bookkeeping a
49|  script can do: scaffold `docs/` and `.okf/` with a `CLAUDE.md` block and a
50|  first decision (ADR 0011), create a new decision or practice with the next
51|  number and its index entry, supersede a decision, list what is due for
52|  review, check indexes and links, and list live and expired handoffs.
53|- **An APM package**, `apm/`, installed by the CLI (ADR 0014). It holds an
54|  audit agent with three review skills (architecture, decision log,
55|  practices), a skill for writing Diataxis docs, `/handoff` and `/continue`,
56|  which write and read back handoffs in `.okf/handoffs/` (ADR 0008), and the
57|  four knowledge rules, and it depends on the okf skills for OKF authoring and
58|  validation. Skills route; `kmctl` decides and writes.
59|  The package also ships, per harness, the SessionStart hook that relays
60|  `kmctl`'s briefing (ADR 0004), okf's MCP server and, for Antigravity, okf's
61|  Stop check (ADR 0018), so APM (Agent Package Manager) installs all of it
62|  (ADR 0020). The user adds the package to `apm.yml` at the CLI's own
63|  version and runs `apm install --target claude` (or `--target
64|  antigravity`); `kmctl plugin patch` then adds only what APM cannot
65|  install yet: the agents translated to Antigravity's format, in
66|  `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` (ADR 0015, ADR 0021). The harnesses are Claude
67|  Code and Antigravity.
68|- **A reusable GitHub Action** (ADR 0005). On every pull request it runs the
69|  deterministic checks for free. The LLM audit is opt-in and reports only.
70|
71|## Invariants
72|
73|Each is `planned` until the test named for it passes, then `enforced`.
74|
75|- **I1. One hook of its own, and it never breaks a session.** kmctl's own
76|  hook is SessionStart, and it exits 0 even when `kmctl` is missing or
77|  fails. In Antigravity kmctl also relays okf's opt-in Stop check, which
78|  APM's copy cannot run there (ADR 0018); it exits 0 and prints `{}` when
79|  okf's script is missing or fails. Status: enforced by
80|  `tests/test_plugin.py` (the package ships one SessionStart hook; it exits
81|  0 without `kmctl` and when it fails) and
82|  `tests/test_antigravity.py` (Antigravity's SessionStart hook prints `{}`
83|  and exits 0 in both cases; the okf Stop relay prints `{}` and exits 0
84|  without a working script).
85|- **I2. Audits never write knowledge.** The audit agent, its skills and the
86|  CI action report findings; they never edit `.okf/` or `docs/` and never
87|  write a `verified` stamp. Status: planned.
88|- **I3. The briefing comes from the CLI and fits a budget.** The hook prints
89|  what `kmctl` prints, so upgrading the CLI updates the briefing, and it
90|  stays under 500 tokens (estimated at four characters a token). Status: enforced by `tests/test_budget.py::test_briefing_token_budget`.
91|- **I4. kmctl reads OKF as it is.** It uses the fields the OKF v0.2 spec
92|  defines (`stale_after`, `verified`, `sources`, `status`) plus the extension
93|  fields an ADR names. The only one is `handoff_key` (ADR 0009); a covers
94|  field is out of scope (ADR 0006).
95|  Status: enforced by `tests/test_okf_fields.py` (written keys, and reads through
96|  `okf.field`).
97|
98|## Values
99|
100|- **Context beats documentation** for agents: what must be known is
101|  injected, not linked.
102|- **Prompts may, code must.** What a script can check, a script checks; the
103|  agent does only the judging.
104|- **Measure before gating.** No new hook or gate without a count showing it
105|  catches something.
106|- **Plain language** in everything kmctl prints and every page it writes.
107|- **Every skill is made with the skill-creator skill** (ADR 0007).
108|
109|## Out of scope for now
110|
111|- A `covers` field mapping concepts to code paths (ADR 0006).
112|- Hooks beyond SessionStart: a nudge after code edits, a reminder at Stop,
113|  a commit gate (ADR 0004).
114|- More harnesses than the two in Parts: opencode, Hermes and others come
115|  later (ADR 0014, ADR 0015).
116|- Writing `verified` stamps from an audit (ADR 0005).

13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|The knowledge setup in loop-harness v2 (docs/ by Diataxis, an .okf/ bundle,
20|rules and skills) worked, and the operator wants it in every repository,
21|including ones that do not run the loop.
22|
23|## Decision
24|
25|- kmctl is a standalone package and repository.
26|- It follows loop-harness ADR 0008: a Typer CLI whose help is written for
27|  agents, that installs its own plugin from the same release, and whose
28|  skills route to CLI verbs instead of carrying logic.
29|
30|Rejected:
31|
32|- Build it into loopctl. Repositories that do not run the loop could not use it.
33|- A plugin with no CLI. The briefing, the bookkeeping verbs and the CI checks
34|  need code that runs the same in every harness and in CI.
35|
36|## Correction, 2026-10-15
37|
38|The record had no Consequences section; this adds it.
39|
40|### Consequences
41|
42|- One release carries both halves: the plugin is package data, and
43|  `kmctl plugin install` stages it stamped with the CLI's version, so
44|  `kmctl plugin status` can report a plugin and CLI that do not match.
45|- Installing the plugin needs the `claude` CLI on PATH, and the hook needs
46|  `kmctl` on PATH; without it the hook prints how to install it.
47|- Skills stay short and call kmctl verbs, so logic lives in tested code.
48|
49|## Correction, 2026-10-16
50|
51|The Consequences said the plugin is package data that `kmctl plugin install`
52|stages stamped with the CLI's version, and that installing it needs the
53|`claude` CLI. Since [ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md) the
54|skills, agent and rules ship as the APM package in `apm/`, whose
55|`apm/apm.yml` carries the release version. `kmctl plugin install --harness
56|claude` writes that package into the repository's apm.yml at the tag
57|`v<cli version>` and installs it with APM, so the CLI still installs the
58|content of its own release, and `kmctl plugin status` compares the ref in
59|`apm.lock.yaml` with the CLI's version. The wheel carries only the skills,
60|for `kmctl briefing`; nothing is staged, and the install needs `uv` rather
61|than `claude` on PATH.
62|
63|## Correction, 2026-10-17
64|
65|`kmctl plugin status`, named in the Consequences and in the 2026-10-16
66|correction, no longer exists: the `kmctl-doctor` ticket that
67|[ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md) planned folded it into
68|`kmctl doctor`. Its `HARNESS.lock` check compares the kmctl ref in
69|`apm.lock.yaml` with this kmctl's version (`src/kmctl/doctor.py`). The
70|decision stands.

12|# ADR 0003: The Claude Code plugin comes first and depends on the okf plugin
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|OKF authoring and validation already exist in the okf plugin by Marco Boffo
20|(github.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills, marketplace scaccogatto). Claude Code
21|supports plugin dependencies
22|(https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-dependencies).
23|
24|## Decision
25|
26|- Build the Claude Code plugin first; other harnesses after it works.
27|- Declare okf as a dependency. It lives in another marketplace, so kmctl's
28|  marketplace.json lists scaccogatto in allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn,
29|  and the dependency is declared in the marketplace entry, so a missing
30|  allowlist refuses the install instead of installing a plugin that then
31|  fails to load.
32|- No version range for now: a range resolves against okf--vX.Y.Z git tags
33|  in the okf repository, and it is not yet checked that those exist.
34|- For other harnesses, kmctl uses the okf author's skills or MCP server
35|  instead of a plugin dependency.
36|
37|Rejected:
38|
39|- Copy the okf skills into kmctl. Two copies drift.
40|- All harnesses at once. Each has its own hook and plugin format; one that
41|  works first shows what the others need.
42|
43|## Correction, 2026-10-15
44|
45|The record had no Consequences section; this adds it.
46|
47|### Consequences
48|
49|- `kmctl plugin install` adds the scaccogatto marketplace before
50|  installing, because `claude plugin install` does not add a dependency's
51|  marketplace by itself.
52|- With no version range, any okf release installs; a breaking okf change
53|  reaches kmctl users without warning.
54|- Only Claude Code is supported so far; other harnesses get the briefing
55|  only if they run `kmctl briefing` themselves.
56|

58|
59|Superseded by [ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md).
60|
61|The other harnesses follow through APM: Antigravity in
62|[ADR 0015](0015-antigravity-gets-skills-and-rules-from-apm-and-a-kmctl-plugin-folder.md).

11|
12|# ADR 0005: Audits report only, and CI runs them in two tiers
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|Knowledge drifts and no deterministic check catches all of it, so an agent
20|has to judge. An agent that both judges and edits the knowledge can quietly
21|make it agree with itself.
22|
23|## Decision
24|
25|- One audit agent uses three skills: architecture review (does the design
26|  match the code), decision-log review (does each decision still hold, or has
27|  a later one or the code overtaken it) and practices review (does each
28|  practice still have the evidence it cites).
29|- It reports findings. It never edits .okf/ or docs/ and never writes a
30|  verified stamp. A person, or an agent the person asks, acts on them.
31|- The reusable GitHub Action has two tiers: the deterministic checks on every
32|  pull request, at no model cost, and the LLM audit only when a repository
33|  opts in. Both report as a job summary or comment.
34|
35|Rejected:
36|
37|- The audit writes verified stamps when a concept passes. The operator chose
38|  report only.
39|
40|## Correction, 2026-10-15
41|
42|The record had no Consequences section; this adds it.
43|
44|### Consequences
45|
46|- The audit skill, its three review skills and the kmctl-auditor agent
47|  write no knowledge; a person or an agent they ask acts on the findings.
48|- Nothing is ever marked verified by an audit, so a concept stays due until
49|  a person checks it.
50|- The GitHub Action runs `kmctl check` and `kmctl review due` and fails
51|  when `kmctl check` fails or `kmctl review due` crashes; due concepts are
52|  reported, never failed.
53|- The action's opt-in `mode: audit` runs the auditor through headless
54|  Claude Code with only Read, Grep, Glob and Agent, on workflow_dispatch or
55|  schedule only, and reports in the job summary and one "Knowledge audit"
56|  issue. It never edits or pushes. It fails when Claude Code errors or
57|  returns no findings, never because a concept drifted.
58|
59|## Correction, 2026-10-15
60|
61|The last Consequence above is out of date. The action's `mode: audit` now
62|runs the auditor through Hermes Agent against any OpenAI-compatible
63|provider, with only kmctl's three read tools (`kmctl_read_file`,
64|`kmctl_search_files`, `kmctl_list_files`), which refuse any path outside the
65|repository. It fails when Hermes errors, runs past its time limit or returns
66|no findings, never because a concept drifted. Why is
67|[ADR 0010](0010-the-ci-audit-runs-hermes-agent-against-any-openai-compatible-provider.md).
68|The report-only rule and the two tiers stand.
69|
70|## Correction, 2026-10-17
71|
72|The 2026-10-15 correction above is out of date. The action's `mode: audit`
73|now runs `action/agent.py`, a standalone PydanticAI agent, against any
74|provider. It reads the repository and the context and skill folders it is
75|given, and can run shell commands so skills' scripts work. Its system prompt
76|says never to change, commit or push a file, and nothing it changes is
77|committed or pushed: the checkout holds no credentials and the GitHub token
78|reaches only the later issue step. It fails when the run errors or passes
79|its time limit, never because a concept drifted. It still runs only on
80|`workflow_dispatch` or `schedule`: `action.yml` refuses any other event
81|before the agent starts. Why is
82|[ADR 0017](0017-the-ci-audit-is-a-standalone-pydanticai-agent-script.md).
83|The report-only rule and the two tiers stand.
[end of file]

3|title: "ADR 0006: Staleness comes from OKF's own fields; a covers field is out of scope"
4|description: "kmctl decides what is due for review from stale_after, verified and sources, which OKF v0.2 already defines; a field mapping concepts to code paths is deferred."

11|
12|# ADR 0006: Staleness comes from OKF's own fields; a covers field is out of scope
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|To list what is due for review, kmctl needs a signal. OKF v0.2 defines
20|stale_after (a date), verified (who confirmed a concept and when) and
21|sources (what it was written from). A covers field mapping a concept to the
22|code it describes would give a sharper signal; the spec allows extension
23|fields.
24|
25|## Decision
26|
27|Use only the spec's fields for now: due when stale_after has passed, when a
28|concept has no verified entry, or when a file in its sources changed in git
29|after its last verified date.
30|
31|Rejected for now:
32|
33|- A covers extension field. It needs every concept tagged, and the operator
34|  wants to keep this simple. Revisit if the spec's fields prove too blunt.
35|
36|## Correction, 2026-10-15
37|
38|The record had no Consequences section; this adds it.
39|
40|### Consequences
41|
42|- `kmctl review due` needs no extra field, so it works on any OKF v0.2
43|  bundle as it is.
44|- A concept with no `verified` entry is always due, so every concept an
45|  agent writes is due until a person verifies it. Handoffs are the
46|  exception: they are due only once their `stale_after` has passed.
47|- The source-changed reason needs full git history; in a shallow clone or
48|  outside git it is skipped with a note.
49|- A code change to a file not listed in a concept's `sources` flags
50|  nothing.
[end of file]

11|
12|# ADR 0008: /handoff and /continue use OKF handoff concepts
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|The operator's memex plugin has /handoff and /continue skills
20|(github.com/JasperHG90/memex, packages/claude-code-plugin/skills).
21|/handoff writes a technical summary of where the work stands: summary, where
22|it stands, next steps, key references. /continue lists recent handoffs as a
23|multi-select, loads the chosen ones, summarizes them together and asks what
24|to do next. memex stores them as notes in its own service.
25|
26|kmctl already has a place for this: .okf/handoffs/, where each note carries a
27|stale_after date.
28|
29|## Decision
30|
31|- /handoff writes a concept in .okf/handoffs/ through kmctl, which fills the
32|  front matter (type, title, description, generated, a stale_after date) and
33|  the index entry. The agent writes the four sections.
34|- /continue asks kmctl for the live handoffs, newest first, offers them as a
35|  multi-select (3 per question plus a more option), loads the chosen ones,
36|  summarizes them together and asks what to do next. It never acts before
37|  the user answers.
38|- Expired handoffs show in kmctl review due, not in /continue.
39|
40|Rejected:
41|
42|- Store handoffs in memex. That ties kmctl to a service a repository may not
43|  run, and the handoff would not travel with the repository.
44|- Keep them outside the bundle (for example in a scratch folder). They would
45|  not be versioned or audited with the rest of the knowledge.
46|
47|## Correction, 2026-10-15
48|
49|The record had no Consequences section; this adds it.
50|
51|### Consequences
52|
53|- `kmctl new handoff` writes the front matter, a `stale_after` 14 days
54|  out and the index entry; `kmctl handoffs` lists the live ones, newest
55|  first, for /continue.
56|- Handoffs are committed with the repository, so they travel with it and
57|  any reader of the bundle sees them.
58|- Expired handoffs stay in the bundle and show in `kmctl review due` until
59|  someone removes them.
60|- Matching a second /handoff in one session to the first needed a key,
61|  which ADR 0009 adds.
[end of file]

- handoff: Write a technical handoff of the current work to .okf/handoffs/ so you, or another agent, can pick it up later with /continue. Use at the end of a work session, when wrapping up a long conversation, or whenever the user says "hand this off", "write up where we are", "save this so I can continue later", "I'll come back to this", or runs /handoff.
  (/home/vscode/kmctl.worktrees/audit-prompts/apm/.apm/skills/handoff/SKILL.md)
- practices-review: Review instructions for .okf/practices/ pages, used through /audit and its kmctl-auditor agent - does each practice still have the count or code site it cites as evidence? Use through /audit; read directly when someone asks how practices are judged.
  (/home/vscode/kmctl.worktrees/audit-prompts/apm/.apm/skills/practices-review/SKILL.md)
- write-docs: Write one page in a repository's docs/ for the people who use the project, filed by Diataxis type (tutorial, how-to, reference or explanation). Use this whenever someone asks to document a feature, write a guide, a getting-started walkthrough, a how-to, a CLI or config reference, or a page explaining why something works the way it does, in a repository with a docs/ folder or a kmctl set-up. Not for decisions, design notes, spikes or handoffs; those go in .okf/.
  (/home/vscode/kmctl.worktrees/audit-prompts/apm/.apm/skills/write-docs/SKILL.md)

## Your report

Finish with a report: a short summary, a checked list and a findings list.

- checked: one entry per page, concept or file you compared, naming what you
  compared it against, with evidence. Something that holds goes here, never
  in findings.
- findings: mismatches only. Each names the claim that does not hold
  (path:line), the lines that contradict it (path:line), and a suggested
  fix. Give each a severity: high for something wrong that someone must
  fix, medium for something that is probably wrong or that you could not
  check, low for something minor, info for a note that needs no fix.

Cite a line as path:line, or a range as path:first-last, with the path
relative to the repository. The report is checked: a citation of a line you
did not read with read_file or get as a search_files hit, or of a line past
the file's end, is sent back.

4|description: "A handoff carries handoff_key, the Claude Code session id, so a second /handoff in one session updates the same concept; it is the only extension field kmctl writes, and invariant I4 now allows fields an ADR names."

11|
12|# ADR 0009: handoff_key is kmctl's one OKF extension field
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|`/handoff` run twice in one session should update one handoff, not add a
20|second (ADR 0008). That needs a key kmctl can match. The Claude Code session
21|id is available to the skill as `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`. OKF v0.2 has no
22|field for it. Invariant I4 said kmctl uses only spec fields, and the
23|operator had said OKF extensions are fine as long as they stay few.
24|
25|## Decision
26|
27|- A handoff written by kmctl carries `handoff_key` in its front matter: the
28|  session id it was written in.
29|- I4 now reads: kmctl uses the spec's fields plus the extension fields an ADR
30|  names. `handoff_key` is the only one.
31|
32|Rejected:
33|
34|- Match on title. Two handoffs in one session with different titles would
35|  not be found, and two sessions with the same title would collide.
36|- Put the key in the file name. File names name an entity, and a session id
37|  in every name makes the section index unreadable.
38|
39|## Consequences
40|
41|- The okf validator accepts unknown keys, so bundles stay conformant.
42|- Adding any other extension field needs its own ADR.
[end of file]

.okf/decisions/0010-the-ci-audit-runs-hermes-agent-against-any-openai-compatible-provider.md, lines 1-79:
1|---
2|type: decision
3|title: "ADR 0010: The CI audit runs Hermes Agent against any OpenAI-compatible provider"
4|description: "The CI audit runs Hermes Agent with a read-only kmctl plugin against any OpenAI-compatible model endpoint, replacing the Claude Code runner, so the audit ties no repository to one model vendor."
5|tags: [adr, decision, ci, audit]
6|generated:
7|  by: claude-opus/5.5
8|  at: 2026-10-15
9|status: deprecated
10|---
11|
12|# ADR 0010: The CI audit runs Hermes Agent against any OpenAI-compatible provider
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|The action's audit mode, added with
20|[ADR 0005](0005-audits-report-only.md)'s two tiers, ran headless Claude Code
21|(`claude -p`) and needed an Anthropic API key. That tied every repository
22|that turns the audit on to one model vendor. The operator asked for the audit
23|to take any provider: Ollama, OpenAI, Bifrost, OpenRouter and others.
24|
25|[Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) runs unattended with
26|`hermes -z` and talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It has no read-only
27|toolset of its own: its `file` toolset includes `write_file` and `patch`, and
28|with no `-t` it offers a terminal and code execution, all approved without a
29|prompt under `-z`. Its own read and search handlers read any file the runner
30|can, and its search passes the pattern to `rg` with no `--`, so a pattern
31|such as `--pre=rm` runs a command.
32|
33|## Decision
34|
35|- The audit runs Hermes Agent, pinned to 0.19.0, with provider `custom` and a
36|  base URL by default, so one setting covers any OpenAI-compatible server.
37|  Hermes' own provider names also pass through.
38|- `action/knowledge-audit.sh` writes the Hermes config into a fresh HOME for
39|  the run. The config names the variable that holds the key, never the key.
40|- The model gets only `kmctl_read_file`, `kmctl_search_files` and
41|  `kmctl_list_files`, from kmctl's own Hermes plugin in
42|  `action/hermes/kmctl-read/`, offered with `-t kmctl_read`. They are plain
43|  Python, start no program, refuse every path that resolves outside the
44|  repository, and match plain text, never a regex. Read-only (I2) holds
45|  because of them.
46|- `timeout` around hermes and `timeout-minutes` on the step bound the run.
47|- The shipped workflow spells out each command as its own step instead of
48|  `uses: ./`, so a reader sees all of it.
49|
50|Rejected:
51|
52|- Keep Claude Code. It needs an Anthropic key, which is the tie the operator
53|  wanted gone.
54|- Use Hermes' built-in `file` toolset with `HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT`. It still
55|  offers the write tools, and its read and search reach outside the
56|  repository, including `/proc/PID/environ`, where the API key is.
57|- Wrap Hermes' own read and search handlers in the plugin. Their search runs
58|  `rg` with the pattern as a bare argument, so a pattern can become a flag.
59|
60|## Consequences
61|
62|- This replaces the Claude Code runner described in ADR 0005's Consequences.
63|  ADR 0005's report-only rule and its two tiers stand.
64|- The action's audit inputs are `provider`, `model`, `base_url` and
65|  `api_key_env`; `anthropic_api_key` is gone.
66|- The model sees only the audited repository, and with it anything the
67|  repository holds, secrets checked into it included.
68|- One Hermes session audits every batch in turn, since Hermes has no
69|  subagent for the auditor. The prompt carries the audit skill, the review
70|  skills the due list needs and the kmctl-auditor instructions as text.
71|- A Hermes upgrade changes the pinned version and reruns the spike that runs
72|  the real script against a fake endpoint.
73|- Hermes refuses an endpoint that reports less than 64K of context, and
74|  Ollama serves a smaller context than the model reports unless `num_ctx` is
75|  set.
76|
77|## Correction, 2026-10-17
78|
79|Superseded by [ADR 0017](0017-the-ci-audit-is-a-standalone-pydanticai-agent-script.md).
[end of file]

.okf/decisions/0011-kmctl-init-writes-knowledge-rules-and-a-claude-md-block-for-claude-code.md, lines 1-156:
1|---
2|type: decision
3|title: "ADR 0011: kmctl init writes knowledge rules and a CLAUDE.md block for Claude Code"
4|description: "kmctl init writes four knowledge rules to .claude/rules/, a kmctl block into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and a first decision; the briefing stays the cross-harness path."
5|tags: [adr, decision, init, rules]
6|generated:
7|  by: claude-opus/5.5
8|  at: 2026-10-15T16:13:16Z
9|status: stable
10|---
11|
12|# ADR 0011: kmctl init writes knowledge rules and a CLAUDE.md block for Claude Code
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-15
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|An agent in a repository set up with `kmctl init` wrote code and left the
20|bundle nearly empty: it made 6 design choices and recorded 1, wrote no
21|architecture page, and left the manifesto's values empty. A fresh
22|`kmctl init` wrote four files and nothing else, so the agent got a briefing
23|and empty templates. In this repository knowledge stays current because of
24|things kmctl did not ship: rule files loaded by path, a `CLAUDE.md` that
25|routes to `.okf/`, and a seeded bundle.
26|
27|[ADR 0002](0002-briefing-and-rules-injected-by-the-cli.md) rejected native
28|rule files per harness, because only some harnesses have them. The briefing
29|it chose is at 526 of its 600 words (I3), so the two rules it lacks
30|(`diagrams-stay-current`, `manifesto-invariants`) do not fit in it.
31|
32|A spike (loop spike `init-seeds-the-habit/1`, one FastAPI task, three runs
33|per arm) compared init plus the briefing with the same plus the seeding
34|below: architecture pages went from 0 of 3 runs to 3 of 3, and decisions
35|recorded from a mean of 3.0 to 4.3.
36|
37|## Decision
38|
39|`kmctl init` also seeds the habit, for Claude Code first
40|([ADR 0003](0003-claude-code-plugin-first-depends-on-okf.md)):
41|
42|- It writes the knowledge rules `okf-bundle`, `docs-layout`,
43|  `diagrams-stay-current` and `manifesto-invariants` to `.claude/rules/`, in
44|  full with their WHY paragraphs and `paths:` front matter, from package data
45|  in `src/kmctl/repo_rules/`. These copies are written for any repository. An
46|  existing file of the same name is kept.
47|- It adds a block between `<!-- kmctl:start -->` and `<!-- kmctl:end -->` to
48|  each `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` that exists, once per real file, so a
49|  `CLAUDE.md` symlinked to `AGENTS.md` gets one block; with neither, it
50|  writes `CLAUDE.md`. The block holds the routing table and three duties:
51|  record each choice as a decision, keep `.okf/architecture/` matching the
52|  code, run `kmctl check` before finishing. A re-run replaces only the block.
53|- It records the decision "Keep project knowledge in an OKF bundle" through
54|  `kmctl new decision`'s writer when no record has that title.
55|- Its last line names the next steps: the manifesto's purpose and
56|  invariants, an architecture page once there is code, and a decision for
57|  each choice.
58|
59|This reverses, for Claude Code only, the alternative ADR 0002 rejected
60|(native rule files per harness). The briefing stays the cross-harness path
61|and keeps its two one-line rules from `src/kmctl/rules/`, unchanged. The
62|CLAUDE.md block carries the gist of the other two rules for any harness that
63|reads `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
64|
65|Rejected:
66|
67|- Add the two rules to the briefing. They take it past its 600-word budget
68|  (I3).
69|- Leave init as it was and rely on the briefing. The spike's unseeded arm
70|  wrote no architecture page in any run.
71|- Write rule files for every harness. Each has its own format, which is
72|  ADR 0002's reason, and the plugin is Claude Code first.
73|
74|## Consequences
75|
76|- `kmctl init` no longer leaves every kept file alone. The exceptions are the
77|  kmctl block in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` and the first decision's index
78|  entry and log line; `ScaffoldResult` and `kmctl init --help` name them.
79|- Two copies of the knowledge rules ship in the package: the briefing's
80|  one-line forms in `src/kmctl/rules/` and the full files in
81|  `src/kmctl/repo_rules/`. A change to a rule changes both.
82|- A repository that edits a seeded rule keeps its edit; init never
83|  overwrites it, so an upgrade does not reach it.
84|- Every new bundle starts with decision 0001, so a user's first
85|  `kmctl new decision` is numbered 0002.
86|
87|## Correction, 2026-10-15
88|
89|The Decision said that with neither `CLAUDE.md` nor `AGENTS.md` init writes
90|`CLAUDE.md`. That left a repository with only `AGENTS.md` without a
91|`CLAUDE.md`, and the operator asked for one whenever it is missing. Claude
92|Code 2.1.300 reads `AGENTS.md` only when there is no `CLAUDE.md`, or when
93|`CLAUDE.md` imports it with `@AGENTS.md`, which loads it once (loop spike
94|`init-claude-md-always/1`). So:
95|
96|- With `AGENTS.md` and no `CLAUDE.md`, init adds the block to `AGENTS.md`
97|  and writes a `CLAUDE.md` holding only `@AGENTS.md`. With neither, it
98|  writes `CLAUDE.md` with the block, as before.
99|- A `CLAUDE.md` with an `@AGENTS.md` line, beside an `AGENTS.md`, never gets
100|  the block, since it already loads `AGENTS.md`'s; a second init changes
101|  nothing.
102|- A file counts as missing only when no directory entry exists. A
103|  `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` symlink that is dangling or resolves outside the
104|  resolved repository root is left alone, with a warning naming the link and
105|  its target, so init never creates or edits a file through it. A symlink
106|  inside the repository is written through once, as before. When `AGENTS.md`
107|  is such a link and there is no `CLAUDE.md`, init writes no `CLAUDE.md` and
108|  the warning says to fix the link.
109|
110|## Correction, 2026-10-15
111|
112|The kmctl block now holds four duties, not three: a new one tells agents to
113|name the code a concept describes with `kmctl new --source` and to give
114|anything time-bound a `--stale-after`, so `kmctl review due` can flag the
115|concept when that code changes or the date passes (ticket new-concept-freshness).
116|
117|## Correction, 2026-10-16
118|
119|The briefing no longer carries the knowledge rules. `kmctl init` writes them
120|to `.claude/rules/`, and those files reach the agent's system prompt anyway,
121|so repeating them only spent the budget. `src/kmctl/rules/` is gone; the
122|briefing keeps one rule the rule files lack (`unverified-is-a-lead`, in
123|`src/kmctl/briefing.py`), and its budget is 500 tokens instead of 600 words
124|(I3). The operator asked for this on 2026-10-16.
125|
126|## Correction, 2026-10-16
127|
128|The Decision said an existing rule file of the same name is kept, and the
129|Consequences said an upgrade does not reach an edited rule. In practice an
130|upgrade reached no copy at all, edited or not, so every repository kept the
131|rules of the kmctl that first set it up. The operator asked for the rules to
132|be overwritten and for a `kmctl update` verb, and rejected tracking hashes to
133|spare edited copies. So:
134|
135|- The four rule files belong to kmctl. Each run of `kmctl init` replaces one
136|  that differs from the packaged copy, edits included, and lists it under
137|  `updated`; one that matches is listed under `skipped` and not rewritten.
138|  Other files in `.claude/rules/` are never read or written. A rule that is a
139|  symlink dangling or pointing outside the repository is left alone with a
140|  warning, as `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are.
141|- `kmctl update` is the same command as `kmctl init`, for users who look for
142|  an update verb after upgrading.
143|- A repository that wants its own version of one of these rules puts it under
144|  another name (ticket update-refreshes-rules).
145|
146|## Correction, 2026-10-16
147|
148|`kmctl init` no longer writes the four knowledge rules, and `kmctl update`
149|no longer refreshes them. Since
150|[ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md) they ship in kmctl's APM
151|package as `apm/.apm/instructions/NAME.instructions.md`, with the same
152|bodies and their `paths:` written as `applyTo:`, and `kmctl plugin install`
153|puts them in `.claude/rules/` through APM, which also replaces an older copy.
154|`src/kmctl/repo_rules/` is gone, and init's last line now starts with
155|`kmctl plugin install --harness claude`. The rest of this record stands: the
156|kmctl block in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, and the first decision.
[end of file]

1|---
2|type: decision
3|title: "ADR 0012: Releases come from CI"
4|description: "A hand-run release workflow opens a version pull request and a tag workflow publishes the GitHub Release; the plugin manifest is the one version source, with no PyPI and no hatch-vcs."
5|tags: [adr, decision, release]
6|generated:
7|  by: claude-opus/5.5
8|  at: 2026-10-16T10:00:25Z
9|status: stable
10|---
11|
12|# ADR 0012: Releases come from CI
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-16
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|kmctl had no releases. On 2026-10-16 the repository had 0 `v*` tags and 0
20|GitHub Releases over 1173 commits on `main`. The version was written twice by
21|hand, `0.1.0` in `pyproject.toml` and in `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
22|nothing built or checked a release, and every install line in the docs
23|followed `main`, so a user could not pin the kmctl they had tested.
24|
25|The plugin ships inside the wheel ([ADR 0001](0001-standalone-cli-installs-its-plugin.md)),
26|and `kmctl plugin install` stamps the CLI's version into the plugin it stages,
27|so one version names both. kmctl installs three ways: `uv tool install` from
28|git at a tag, `uv build`, and `action.yml`, which runs `uv tool install` on the
29|action's own checkout. GitHub hands an action to a workflow as a download with
30|no `.git` folder.
31|
32|## Decision
33|
34|The plugin manifest, `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, is the one place the
35|version is written. `pyproject.toml` declares the version dynamic and reads it
36|with hatchling's `regex` version source, so every build, with or without git
37|history, carries the manifest's version (loop spike `release-flow/1` built a
38|wheel, an sdist, a git install at a tag and an install from a `git archive`
39|folder, and all printed the manifest's version).
40|
41|Two workflows make a release, each command a step of its own:
42|
43|- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, run by hand, works out the version from the
44|  newest `v*` tag (`scripts/next_release_version.py`), refuses a real run off
45|  `main` or a tag that exists, runs the lint and the tests, and builds and
46|  checks the wheel at that version (`twine check`, `scripts/check_wheel.py`,
47|  `scripts/smoke_wheel.py`). A dry run, the default, stops there. A real run
48|  commits `scripts/release.py set` (the manifest, and the five install lines
49|  in the docs pinned to the new tag) on `release/vX.Y.Z` and opens the version
50|  pull request. Merging it is the approval.
51|- `.github/workflows/release-tag.yml` runs when a push to `main` changes the
52|  manifest. When the version went up, it builds and checks the release files
53|  first, then pushes the annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` and publishes a GitHub Release
54|  with the wheel, the sdist and `SHA256SUMS`.
55|
56|Rejected: hatch-vcs, which reads the version from the git tag. `action.yml`
57|installs kmctl from a download with no `.git`, where hatch-vcs has no tag to
58|read and falls back to a placeholder version, so the action would report the
59|wrong kmctl.
60|
61|Rejected: publishing to PyPI. The operator chose GitHub Releases only; users
62|install from git at a tag, and the Release holds the files for anyone who
63|wants them.
64|
65|## Consequences
66|
67|- `kmctl --version`, the plugin stamp and the action all report the manifest's
68|  version, and a version change is a one-line diff that `release-tag.yml`
69|  acts on.
70|- The bump job opens its pull request with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which needs the
71|  repository setting
72|  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"
73|  (Settings, Actions, General). It was off; the operator turned it
74|  on on 2026-10-16 instead of adding a token secret. If it is turned off, the
75|  bump job deletes its branch and fails, naming the setting.
76|- A pull request opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow, so the version
77|  pull request shows no checks; `release.yml` runs the lint and the tests
78|  itself before it opens one.
79|- The first release needs `--version`, since no tag exists to count from.
80|  Until it lands, the docs' `uv tool install` lines name no ref and the
81|  action's `uses:` lines name `@main`.
82|- A hand edit to the manifest's version on `main` also releases, through the
83|  same build-and-check steps.
84|
85|## Correction, 2026-10-16
86|
87|The one version source is now `apm/apm.yml`, kmctl's APM package, not the
88|plugin manifest, which is gone with `plugin/`
89|([ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md)). `pyproject.toml`'s
90|hatchling `regex` source reads its `version:` line, `scripts/release.py set`
91|writes it and copies it to the root `apm.yml`, `current` refuses when the two
92|differ, and `release.yml` and `release-tag.yml` stage and watch `apm/apm.yml`
93|instead of the manifest. The rest of the release flow is unchanged.
94|
95|## Correction, 2026-10-17
96|
97|The docs hold six install lines for `scripts/release.py set` to point at
98|the release tag, not five: the CI how-to's audit workflow now has a second
99|job, which uses the action in `mode: publish`
100|([ADR 0017](0017-the-ci-audit-is-a-standalone-pydanticai-agent-script.md)).
[end of file]

12|# ADR 0013: kmctl installs through APM too
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-16
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|On 2026-10-16 kmctl's skills and agent reached a repository one way:
20|`kmctl plugin install`, which stages `plugin/` stamped with the CLI's version
21|and installs it as the Claude Code plugin `kmctl@kmctl`, after adding the okf
22|plugin's marketplace
23|([ADR 0001](0001-standalone-cli-installs-its-plugin.md),
24|[ADR 0003](0003-claude-code-plugin-first-depends-on-okf.md)). The operator
25|asked for an install through APM, Microsoft's Agent Package Manager
26|(`apm-cli` 0.33.0), in release 0.2.0.
27|
28|APM 0.33.0 reads `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` as a Claude plugin and
29|installs `plugin/` as a git subfolder package: the 7 skills and the
30|`kmctl-auditor` agent byte for byte into `.claude/`, and the SessionStart hook
31|into `.claude/settings.json`. An apm.yml that declares dependencies inside
32|`plugin/` makes APM read agents only from `.apm/agents/`, so the agent is
33|dropped. A consumer of a subfolder package gets none of the root apm.yml's
34|dependencies, which are this repository's 16 dev rules and skills. APM
35|requires a `version:` in every apm.yml.
36|
37|5 of the 7 skills and the agent run a `kmctl` command, so APM can deliver the
38|files but cannot make them work without the CLI.
39|
40|## Decision
41|
42|- `apm/apm.yml`, a folder holding only that file, is kmctl's APM package. It
43|  depends on `{git: parent, path: plugin}` and on `scaccogatto/okf-skills`
44|  pinned to a commit. A consumer adds one entry,
45|  `JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm#vX.Y.Z`, and gets kmctl's skills, agent
46|  and hook plus okf's skills, agents and Stop hook.
47|- `plugin/` keeps no apm.yml, so the agent is not dropped.
48|- `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` stays the one version source
49|  ([ADR 0012](0012-releases-come-from-ci.md)). The root `apm.yml` and
50|  `apm/apm.yml` carry copies: `scripts/release.py set` writes them, and
51|  `scripts/release.py current` refuses when a copy differs.
52|- APM is a second route beside `kmctl plugin install`, the operator's choice
53|  on 2026-10-16. `kmctl plugin install` stays the main route.
54|
55|Rejected:
56|
57|- Replace `kmctl plugin install` with APM. APM installs the files but not the
58|  CLI, and it has no counterpart to ADR 0001's version check: the CLI
59|  installs the plugin of its own release, and `kmctl plugin status` reports
60|  when the two versions differ. APM cannot see the CLI's version, so it
61|  would install skills that may not match the `kmctl` on PATH.
62|- Put an apm.yml in `plugin/`. APM then drops the agent.
63|
64|## Consequences
65|
66|- The APM route skips ADR 0001's version check. A user installs the CLI with
67|  `uv tool install` at the same tag as the APM package, and nothing checks
68|  that they match.
69|- The APM route leaves out the kmctl CLI, and okf's MCP server, which APM
70|  skips as a transitive dependency unless the consumer runs
71|  `apm install --trust-transitive-mcp` or lists `scaccogatto/okf-skills`
72|  directly.
73|- Project scope only: no `apm install -g`. APM refuses `git: parent` at user
74|  scope.
75|- While the kmctl repository is private, APM needs GitHub auth with access to
76|  it.
77|- `docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md` documents the route, and
78|  `scripts/release.py set` moves its `#vX.Y.Z` pin with each release.
79|  `tests/test_apm_package.py` checks the package against `plugin/` and
80|  installs it into a scratch consumer with APM 0.33.0.
81|
82|## Correction, 2026-10-16
83|
84|Superseded by [ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md).
[end of file]

15|# ADR 0014: APM is the only install route
16|
17|- Status: Accepted
18|- Date: 2026-10-16
19|
20|## Context
21|
22|On 2026-10-16 a repository got kmctl's pieces in two commands and through
23|three routes, each with part of them. `kmctl plugin install` staged
24|`plugin/` and installed it as the Claude Code plugin `kmctl@kmctl`
25|([ADR 0001](0001-standalone-cli-installs-its-plugin.md),
26|[ADR 0003](0003-claude-code-plugin-first-depends-on-okf.md)): the 7 skills,
27|the audit agent and the SessionStart hook, but none of the 4 knowledge rules.
28|The APM package in `apm/` ([ADR 0013](0013-kmctl-installs-through-apm-too.md))
29|gave the same, also without the rules. The rules came only from `kmctl init`
30|([ADR 0011](0011-kmctl-init-writes-knowledge-rules-and-a-claude-md-block-for-claude-code.md)).
31|The claude plugin route works only for Claude Code.
32|
33|The operator asked (2026-10-16) for kmctl to reach more harnesses than Claude
34|Code through APM (Microsoft's Agent Package Manager, `apm-cli` 0.33.0), with
35|`kmctl plugin install` kept as a thin wrapper around it, and hooks, rules,
36|skills and agents all delivered. This is the first of three tickets in that
37|work; it does Claude Code on the new layout.
38|
39|What APM 0.33.0 does, from the ticket's spikes:
40|
41|- A package `apm/apm.yml` with the skills, agent and rules as
42|  `*.instructions.md` under `apm/.apm/` installs the 7 skills and the agent
43|  byte for byte, and the rules into `.claude/rules/` with their `paths:`
44|  equal to the comma-joined `applyTo:` (spike:apm-only-install/1).
45|- `apm install -g` of that package writes the same under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
46|  (default `~/.claude/`), the folders Claude Code reads at user scope
47|  (spike:apm-only-install/2).
48|- The CLI form `apm install PACKAGE` cannot name a subfolder of a repository
49|  on a host other than GitHub, and APM writes `targets:` into apm.yml only
50|  when it creates the file (spike:apm-only-install/1, spike:kmctl-doctor/1).
51|- APM overwrites a rule file it did not write, but leaves a skill folder it
52|  did not write in place, printing only a count, `N file skipped -- local
53|  files exist` (spike:apm-only-install/3, spike:apm-only-install/5).
54|- APM skips okf's MCP server, because okf-skills is a dependency of kmctl's
55|  package, and okf's entry points at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, which only a
56|  Claude plugin fills in.
57|- Old installs leave duplicates. Swapping an ADR 0013 apm.yml entry keeps the
58|  old package's SessionStart hook; only `apm uninstall` removes it
59|  (spike:apm-only-install/6). Uninstalling the claude plugin `kmctl@kmctl`
60|  leaves `okf@scaccogatto` enabled until `claude plugin prune`
61|  (spike:apm-only-install/7).
62|
63|## Decision
64|
65|The APM package in `apm/` is the only way kmctl's skills, agent and rules
66|reach a repository. `kmctl plugin install --harness claude` installs it:
67|
68|- **The package.** `apm/apm.yml` names kmctl, carries the release version
69|  and depends only on `scaccogatto/okf-skills` pinned to a commit. The 7
70|  skills sit in `apm/.apm/skills/`, the auditor in `apm/.apm/agents/`, and the
71|  4 knowledge rules in `apm/.apm/instructions/` as `NAME.instructions.md`, with
72|  their old `paths:` written as a comma-joined `applyTo:`. `plugin/`,
73|  `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `src/kmctl/repo_rules/` are gone.
74|- **The install.** `kmctl plugin install --harness claude` writes the entry
75|  `{git: SOURCE, path: apm, ref: v<cli version>}` and the harnesses as
76|  `targets:` into the repository's apm.yml, keeping its other entries and
77|  comments, then runs `uvx --from apm-cli==0.33.0 apm install --target claude`.
78|  The ref is the CLI's own version, so the CLI still installs the content of
79|  its own release (ADR 0001). `--harness` takes a comma list; `claude` is the
80|  only value so far. `--source GIT_URL` (default
81|  `https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management.git`) points it at a
82|  fork, a local server or an unreleased tree; the operator chose an option
83|  over an environment variable. `kmctl plugin update` runs the same steps.
84|  `--scope user` runs `apm install -g` with the entry in `~/.apm/apm.yml`.
85|- **The hook.** kmctl writes the one SessionStart hook itself, merging one
86|  entry that runs `kmctl briefing` into `.claude/settings.json` (at user
87|  scope, the settings file under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). It finds its own entry
88|  by that command, replaces it in place, and leaves every other key and hook
89|  alone. ADR 0004 still holds.
90|- **okf's MCP server.** kmctl declares it too: one server, `okf-bundle`, in
91|  the repository's `.mcp.json` (at user scope with `claude mcp add-json
92|  --scope user`), running `uv run` of okf's `okf_mcp.py` at the pinned commit
93|  through a short `sh` launcher that finds the nearest `.okf/` folder. When
94|  another server already runs `okf_mcp.py`, kmctl adds none and says which it
95|  kept.
96|- **Skipped files.** When APM says it left local files in place, the install
97|  fails with the skill folders it worked out from `apm.lock.yaml` and the fix,
98|  `kmctl plugin install --force`, which passes `--force` to APM and replaces
99|  those folders whole. Without `--force` kmctl never overwrites a file the
100|  user wrote.
101|- **Old installs.** Before writing apm.yml, the install runs `apm uninstall`
102|  on an entry that names `JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm` another way.
103|  Once `apm install` has succeeded, it removes the claude plugin
104|  `kmctl@kmctl` where it applies (`claude plugin uninstall`, then
105|  `claude plugin prune` and `claude plugin marketplace remove kmctl`, at the
106|  plugin's scope), so a failed install leaves the old plugin working; it
107|  skips this with a note when `claude` is not on PATH. The operator chose to
108|  remove old installs rather than only report them.
109|- **The rules leave `kmctl init`.** Init no longer writes the 4 rules; its
110|  next step names `kmctl plugin install`. This replaces ADR 0011's first
111|  decision bullet and its rule refresh; its CLAUDE.md block and first
112|  decision stay.
113|- **One version source.** `apm/apm.yml`'s `version:` replaces the plugin
114|  manifest as the one place the version is written
115|  ([ADR 0012](0012-releases-come-from-ci.md)). The wheel carries only the
116|  skills folder, for `kmctl briefing` to list.
117|- `kmctl plugin status` reports the kmctl ref in `apm.lock.yaml` against the
118|  CLI version and whether the hook is there, each problem naming its fix.
119|
120|This supersedes ADR 0013 (APM as a second route) and ADR 0003 (a Claude Code
121|plugin with an okf plugin dependency).
122|
123|Rejected:
124|
125|- Keep the claude plugin route beside APM. Two routes deliver different
126|  pieces, and only APM can serve a second harness.
127|- Let APM install the hook from the package. An ADR 0013 swap showed APM
128|  leaves a package's old hook behind, and APM writes hooks only in the shapes
129|  it knows; kmctl finding its own entry by its command keeps exactly one.
130|- Run `apm install JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm#vX` without writing
131|  apm.yml. It cannot point at another host's subfolder, so `--source` and the
132|  integration test would not work, and APM would not record the targets.
133|- Uninstall `okf@scaccogatto` by name when removing the old plugin. Prune
134|  removes it only when kmctl alone pulled it in, so an okf the user installed
135|  on purpose stays.
136|
137|## Consequences
138|
139|- One command gives a Claude Code repository everything: the 7 skills, the
140|  agent, the 4 rules, okf's skills, the hook and okf's MCP server.
141|- Every install needs `uv` on PATH, since kmctl runs APM with `uvx`; the
142|  `claude` CLI is needed only at user scope for the MCP server and to remove
143|  the old plugin.
144|- An apm.yml entry added by hand still gets the skills, agent and rules, but
145|  no SessionStart hook and no okf MCP server;
146|  `docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md` says so and how to get them.
147|- Claude Code asks the user to approve a project `.mcp.json` server once.
148|- The next tickets build on this: `antigravity-harness` adds `--harness
149|  antigravity` and reuses the MCP launcher, and `kmctl-doctor` folds
150|  `kmctl plugin status` into `kmctl doctor`, reusing the hook and MCP writers.
151|- `tests/test_plugin.py` checks the install with fake `uvx` and `claude`, and
152|  `tests/test_apm_package.py` runs it with the real APM 0.33.0 against this
153|  tree served from a local git server.
154|
155|Supersedes [ADR 0013](0013-kmctl-installs-through-apm-too.md).
156|
157|Supersedes [ADR 0003](0003-claude-code-plugin-first-depends-on-okf.md).
158|
159|### Amended, 2026-10-17
160|
161|[ADR 0020](0020-apm-installs-the-hooks-mcp-server-and-rules-kmctl-patches-the-rest.md):
162|kmctl's package now ships the SessionStart hooks, okf's MCP server and the
163|rules for each harness, and APM writes them; kmctl writes only the
164|Antigravity agents and removes APM's broken okf Stop handler.
165|
166|### Amended again, 2026-10-17
167|
168|[ADR 0021](0021-apm-installs-kmctl-s-package-kmctl-plugin-patch-adds-the-rest.md):
169|users install, upgrade and remove the package with APM's own verbs;
170|`kmctl plugin install`, `update` and `remove` are gone, and
171|`kmctl plugin patch` adds what APM cannot install yet.
[end of file]

15|# ADR 0015: Antigravity gets skills and rules from APM and a kmctl plugin folder
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|[ADR 0016](0016-antigravity-rules-come-from-the-kmctl-plugin-folder.md)
20|moves the rules into kmctl's plugin folder: APM's copies in `.agents/rules/`
21|never reach an Antigravity session. [ADR 0018](0018-kmctl-runs-okf-s-stop-check-for-antigravity.md)
22|has kmctl run okf's Stop check, whose APM copy fails in Antigravity.
23|
24|[ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md) made APM (`apm-cli`
25|0.33.0) the one install route and served Claude Code only. The operator asked
26|(2026-10-16) for kmctl's skills, rules, agent and hook to reach Antigravity
27|(Google's agent IDE and CLI, `agy` 1.4.0) through the same route, with
28|`kmctl plugin install` a thin wrapper that takes the harness.
29|
30|What APM and Antigravity do, from the ticket's spikes and APM's
31|`apm_cli/integration/targets.py`:
32|
33|- With `--target antigravity` APM writes skills to `.agents/skills/` and the
34|  rules to `.agents/rules/`. It writes no agents and no MCP config Antigravity
35|  reads: Antigravity reads MCP servers only from
36|  `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` or a plugin's `mcp_config.json`. At user
37|  scope APM writes no rules and no hooks for Antigravity.
38|- Antigravity loads a plugin from `plugins/NAME/` under a customization root
39|  such as the workspace `.agents/`, but only in a trusted workspace
40|  (`trustedWorkspaces`, matched exactly; spike:antigravity-harness/3). agy
41|  registered the hook of such a plugin (spike:antigravity-harness/4); whether
42|  the hook fires and the MCP server starts could not be seen on this account.
43|- An Antigravity hooks.json maps names to hooks; SessionStart holds a flat
44|  list of handlers. A hook gets a JSON object on stdin whose `workspacePaths`
45|  names the workspace, and its stdout must be JSON.
46|- Antigravity agents name Antigravity tools (`view_file`, `grep_search`,
47|  `find_by_name`, `list_dir`, `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`,
48|  `run_command`) and take `mainAgent`, `subagent`, `model` and
49|  `commandExecutionPolicy`; Claude Code agents name Claude tools.
50|- `uv run` of okf's `okf_mcp.py` from its raw GitHub URL at the pinned commit
51|  starts okf's MCP server, given the `.okf` folder as its argument
52|  (spike:antigravity-harness/1).
53|
54|## Decision
55|
56|`kmctl plugin install --harness antigravity` runs the same APM install as for
57|Claude Code, `apm install --target antigravity` (both harnesses with
58|`--harness claude,antigravity`), then writes the folder
59|`.agents/plugins/kmctl/`, which kmctl alone owns and replaces whole on every
60|run:
61|
62|- `plugin.json`, naming the plugin `kmctl`.
63|- `hooks.json` with one named hook, `kmctl-briefing`, holding one
64|  SessionStart handler. It runs `kmctl briefing --format antigravity`, which
65|  prints the briefing as `{"injectSteps": [{"systemMessage": {"systemMessage":
66|  TEXT}}]}` and reads the repository from `workspacePaths[0]` on stdin,
67|  falling back to `--path`. When kmctl is missing or fails, the handler prints
68|  `{}` and exits 0, so ADR 0004's one hook still never blocks.
69|- `agents/`: kmctl's auditor and okf's `bundle-weaver` and `event-analyzer`
70|  (read from `apm_modules/scaccogatto/okf-skills/agents/`), translated from
71|  Claude Code's format at install time. The tool map is: Read to `view_file`,
72|  Grep to `grep_search`, Glob to `find_by_name` and `list_dir`, Write to
73|  `write_to_file`, Edit to `replace_file_content`, Bash to `run_command`.
74|  Each agent gets `mainAgent: false`, `subagent: true`, `model: inherit`, and
75|  `commandExecutionPolicy: "off"` when it has no Bash; `color`, `effort` and
76|  a named model are dropped and the body is copied unchanged. A Claude tool
77|  missing from the map makes the install refuse and name it. The wheel now
78|  carries the agents folder as well as the skills.
79|- `mcp_config.json` declaring okf's MCP server as `bundle`, run with `uv run`
80|  from the pinned raw URL through ADR 0014's `sh` launcher, which walks up to
81|  the first `.okf/` from the repository above the plugin folder (when
82|  Antigravity sets `PLUGIN_ROOT`) and then from the working folder.
83|
84|`kmctl plugin status --harness antigravity` compares every file in the folder
85|with what this kmctl writes and names each missing, extra or different one
86|with the fix. Antigravity is installed per repository only; `--scope user`
87|with it is refused, because APM writes no rules or hooks there.
88|
89|Rejected:
90|
91|- `agy plugin install` of okf-skills. It kept `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, the
92|  Claude-shaped hooks.json and Claude-format agents, and
93|  `agy plugin validate` counted 0 hooks and 0 agents.
94|- A user-level plugin under `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`. The workspace folder
95|  loads from a trusted repository (spike:antigravity-harness/3) and keeps the
96|  install to the repository, as APM's rules are.
97|- Shipping agents already in Antigravity's format. Two copies of each agent
98|  would drift; one Claude-format source and a translator keep one.
99|
100|## Consequences
101|
102|- Antigravity loads `.agents/` only once the repository folder is trusted;
103|  the install's last step and the install how-to say so, and `kmctl doctor`
104|  is to check it.
105|- okf's MCP server needs `uv` on PATH; when no `.okf/` is found it starts and
106|  reports no bundle, which costs okf's three read-only tools only.
107|- `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` is rebuilt from `apm_modules/`, which is
108|  git-ignored, so a fresh clone needs `kmctl plugin install --harness
109|  antigravity` before status reports the folder as current.
110|- Whether the hook fires and the MCP server starts in a live session is still
111|  unseen; the ticket antigravity-live-check is for checking it on an
112|  eligible account.
113|- The manifesto names Antigravity as a harness kmctl installs for.
114|
115|## Correction, 2026-10-17
116|
117|`kmctl plugin status --harness antigravity`, named in the Decision and the
118|Consequences, no longer exists; `kmctl doctor` took over its checks. Its
119|`antigravity.plugin` check compares the files in `.agents/plugins/kmctl/`
120|with what this kmctl writes, through `antigravity.plugin_problems`

16|# ADR 0016: Antigravity rules come from the kmctl plugin folder
17|
18|## Context
19|
20|[ADR 0015](0015-antigravity-gets-skills-and-rules-from-apm-and-a-kmctl-plugin-folder.md)
21|left the rules for Antigravity to APM, which writes them to `.agents/rules/`.
22|The first live agy session (agy 1.4.0, `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, 2026-10-17)
23|showed that none of the four rules reached it:
24|
25|- APM 0.33.0, the newest release, writes Antigravity rules in Windsurf's
26|  form. A rule with several globs gets `globs:` as a YAML list, and agy
27|  refuses the file ("cannot unmarshal !!seq into string"). Three of the four
28|  rules have several globs.
29|- agy matches a glob that holds a `/` against the file's absolute path, so a
30|  glob relative to the repository, such as `.okf/**` or `docs/**`, never
31|  matches. `**/.okf/**` matches inside the hidden `.okf/` folder, and a glob
32|  without a `/` matches the file name (spike:antigravity-rules/3).
33|- agy reads several globs from one comma-separated string; a `{a,b}` brace
34|  pattern never matches. It loads glob rules from a plugin's `rules/` folder.
35|
36|## Decision
37|
38|kmctl writes the rules for Antigravity itself, as it writes the agents:
39|`.agents/plugins/kmctl/rules/NAME.md` for each
40|`apm/.apm/instructions/NAME.instructions.md`, which the wheel now carries
41|beside the agents. `applyTo` becomes `trigger: glob` and `globs:` as one
42|comma-separated string, each glob given a leading `**/`; an instruction
43|without `applyTo` becomes `trigger: always_on`. The body is copied
44|unchanged.
45|
46|After APM's install, kmctl deletes the rule files the lock lists for kmctl's
47|package under `.agents/rules/`, so agy loads each rule once and logs no
48|parse error. APM writes them back on the next install and removes nothing
49|else because of it, and `apm uninstall` still cleans up
50|(spike:antigravity-rules/2). Other packages' rules stay. `kmctl doctor`
51|checks the rules with the rest of the plugin folder (`antigravity.plugin`)
52|and no longer expects kmctl's rules in `.agents/rules/`
53|(`antigravity.files`).
54|
55|Rejected:
56|
57|- Rewriting APM's files in `.agents/rules/` in place. Their hashes would no
58|  longer match the lock, so doctor would fail and a later APM install could
59|  treat them as local edits.
60|- Waiting for APM to fix its Antigravity writer. The newest APM has the same
61|  writer, and the rules would stay dead until then.
62|
63|## Consequences
64|
65|- Antigravity sessions get the four rules; the Claude Code rules are
66|  unchanged.
67|- The `**/` prefix also matches folders of the same name deeper in the
68|  repository, such as a nested `docs/`; the rules are guidance, so that is
69|  harmless.
70|- A bare `apm install` puts APM's broken copies back until the next
71|  `kmctl plugin install`.
72|
73|## Correction, 2026-10-17
74|
75|Superseded by [ADR 0020](0020-apm-installs-the-hooks-mcp-server-and-rules-kmctl-patches-the-rest.md).
[end of file]

12|# ADR 0017: The CI audit is a standalone PydanticAI agent script
13|
14|- Status: Accepted
15|- Date: 2026-10-17
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|[ADR 0010](0010-the-ci-audit-runs-hermes-agent-against-any-openai-compatible-provider.md)
20|ran the CI audit through Hermes Agent: a bash script built one prompt per
21|batch of due concepts, pasted the audit skill, a review skill and the
22|auditor's instructions into it, and parsed a JSON block out of Hermes' free
23|text. It could do only the knowledge audit. Much of the script fenced Hermes
24|in (its own HOME, unset `HERMES_*` variables, a write-safe root), and the
25|batching existed because a prompt went to Hermes as one command-line
26|argument.
27|
28|On 2026-10-17 the operator asked for a simple, adjustable agent instead: a
29|user message and an optional system prompt, both with defaults; any provider;
30|extra folders a workflow fetches, such as enterprise architecture docs; skills
31|the agent finds and uses as it needs them, scripts included; a report kept as
32|an artifact and posted to GitHub. They asked for Python only, separate from
33|kmctl, as one standalone script.
34|
35|## Decision
36|
37|- `action/agent.py` is one Python script. Its dependencies are declared
38|  inline (PEP 723) and `uv run --script` runs it. It does not import kmctl,
39|  and kmctl does not depend on it; PydanticAI is only a dev dependency, so
40|  the tests can import the script.
41|- It runs one PydanticAI agent. `--prompt` or `--prompt-file` is the task and
42|  `--system-prompt-file` replaces the system prompt. The defaults are the
43|  kmctl knowledge audit (the audit skill, with the kmctl-auditor's
44|  instructions) and a system prompt that lists the folders the agent can read
45|  and its skills.
46|- `--model` takes PydanticAI's `provider:model` name, and `--base-url` with
47|  `--api-key-env` reaches any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so no vendor is
48|  required (spike:standalone-agent/2 ran tools and a typed report through
49|  Gemini's OpenAI-compatible URL).
50|- The agent reads, searches and lists files in the repository, every
51|  `--context` folder and every `--skills` folder, and nowhere else. The
52|  system prompt lists each skill's name and description from its SKILL.md,
53|  and the agent reads the rest when a skill fits.
54|- It also has `run_shell`, so it can run the scripts skills ship and
55|  commands such as `kmctl review due`. Commands get a clean environment:
56|  PATH, HOME and the locale, with no API key and no GitHub token.
57|- It returns a typed `Report` (summary and findings, each with a title,
58|  severity, path, summary and evidence). `run` writes `report.json`,
59|  `report.md` and `transcript.json` to `--out`, and the workflow uploads that
60|  folder as an artifact.
61|- It refuses to start when `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set or git config
62|  holds checkout's token. Posting stays in a separate step, the only one
63|  given the token.
64|
65|Rejected:
66|
67|- Keep Hermes. It needs a fence of environment tricks, takes the prompt as
68|  one argument, returns free text, and cannot take a user's own task.
69|- Google ADK. It has a skill toolset, but it is built Gemini-first, reaches
70|  other providers only through LiteLLM and pulls in a large dependency tree.
71|- DSPy. It optimises prompts through typed signatures; a user cannot simply
72|  hand it a system prompt.
73|- A `kmctl agent` command. The operator wanted the agent separate from
74|  kmctl, so kmctl's users do not install an agent framework.
75|- Read-only tools only. The operator wants skills' scripts to run.
76|
77|## Consequences
78|
79|- This replaces ADR 0010. ADR 0005's report-only rule stands: the system
80|  prompt says never to change, commit or push a file, the checkout keeps no
81|  credentials, and nothing the agent changes is committed or pushed.
82|- Shell commands run as the same user as the script, so a command can still
83|  read the API key from the script's own `/proc/PID/environ`. Use a key
84|  scoped to the audit, with a spending limit. The GitHub token is never in
85|  the agent's step, so no command can reach it.
86|- `action/knowledge-audit.sh`, `action/audit-batches.py`,
87|  `action/audit-report.py` and the `kmctl-read` Hermes plugin are gone, with
88|  their tests. `action/knowledge-audit-issue.sh` now posts the report the
89|  agent wrote.
90|- The action's audit inputs are `model`, `base_url`, `api_key_env`,
91|  `prompt`, `prompt_file`, `system_prompt_file`, `context`, `skills` and
92|  `timeout`; `provider` is gone, folded into `model`.
93|- The agent works through the due list in one run; there is no batching.
94|  A long audit is bounded by `--timeout` and `--max-requests`.
95|- Posting only above a severity and mentioning the CODEOWNERS owners is the
96|  `agent-publish` ticket.
97|
98|Supersedes [ADR 0010](0010-the-ci-audit-runs-hermes-agent-against-any-openai-compatible-provider.md).
99|
100|## Correction, 2026-10-17
101|
102|`action/knowledge-audit-issue.sh` is gone. `action/agent.py publish` posts
103|the report, and it runs in a separate job: `mode: publish` in `action.yml`,
104|and the `publish` job in `.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml`. The
105|agent's shell runs as the runner's user, so any later step in the same job
106|could run code it changed. A GitHub-hosted runner gives each job a fresh
107|machine, and setup-uv's cache is off in both jobs, so the publish job gets
108|nothing from the agent's job but the `agent-report` artifact, which it
109|validates as a `Report`. That holds only on GitHub-hosted runners; a
110|self-hosted runner that reuses its machine between jobs does not give it.
111|
112|`publish` opens or updates one issue when a finding is at or above
113|`--min-severity` (default medium). On an update it replaces the body and adds
114|a comment, since GitHub notifies a mention when it is posted, not when a
115|body is edited. It @-mentions the owners of the last `*` rule in CODEOWNERS
116|or the `--mention` names, and below the threshold it closes the open issue
117|with a comment. When the audit job fails, the publish job is skipped and the
118|issue stays as it was.
119|
120|## Correction, 2026-10-17
121|
122|A live run returned one `info` finding per concept saying it held, and 18
123|of its 61 citations named lines the agent had neither read nor found by
124|search, so "holds" meant little. The `Report` now has a `checked` list,
125|one entry per thing compared with what it was compared against, and
126|`findings` holds mismatches only: each names the claim (`path:line`), the
127|lines that contradict it and a suggested fix. The script records every line
128|range `read_file` returns and every line `search_files` returns, and sends
129|the report back to the agent while it cites any other line, or a line past
130|the file's end. After five retries the run stops with exit 1, names the
131|citations and writes no report. Lines seen only in `run_shell` output do
132|not count, so a finding about a command cites the source that defines it.
[end of file]
