16|# ADR 0018: kmctl runs okf's Stop check for Antigravity
17|
18|## Context
19|
20|okf-skills ships a Stop hook, `okf-stop-check.sh`, that keeps an agent from
21|stopping when tracked files changed and nothing under `.okf/` did. It does
22|nothing unless the bundle opts in with `upkeep: enforced` in
23|`.okf/index.md`. [ADR 0015](0015-antigravity-gets-skills-and-rules-from-apm-and-a-kmctl-plugin-folder.md)
24|left okf's hooks to APM. The first live agy session (agy 1.4.0,
25|2026-10-17) showed APM's copy never works in Antigravity:
26|
27|- APM 0.33.0 merges it into `.agents/hooks.json` as
28|  `bash ".agents/hooks/okf-skills/hooks/okf-stop-check.sh"`, a path from
29|  the repository root, but agy runs a hook in the folder holding its
30|  hooks.json. The script is not found, and agy logs a failed hook (exit
31|  127) at the end of every turn in every repository.
32|- The script reads `.okf/` and runs git from its working folder, so it
33|  needs the repository root.
34|- It prints Claude Code's `{"decision": "block"}`. agy keeps the agent
35|  going only on `"decision": "continue"`; any other value lets it stop.
36|- agy's Stop input carries `executionNum`, which counts from 0 within each
37|  turn and starts again at 0 on the next turn of the same conversation
38|  (spike:antigravity-okf-stop-hook/1, /3). A plugin Stop handler that
39|  prints `continue` sends agy back into the loop with its reason
40|  (spike:antigravity-okf-stop-hook/2).
41|
42|## Decision
43|
44|The operator chose (2026-10-17) to relay okf's check in Antigravity rather
45|than leave it Claude-only, although it makes kmctl write a Stop hook there,
46|which [ADR 0004](0004-sessionstart-is-the-only-hook.md) and invariant I1 had ruled
47|out for kmctl's own nudges. The check stays okf's: opt-in per bundle, okf's
48|script and okf's reason. I1 now says kmctl's own hook is SessionStart and
49|that it relays this one check in Antigravity.
50|
51|The plugin folder's `hooks.json` gets a second named hook,
52|`kmctl-okf-stop`, with one Stop handler. On the first stop of a turn
53|(`executionNum` 0, as okf's own `stop_hook_active` guard allows one
54|re-entry in Claude Code) it changes to the repository root, three levels
55|above the plugin folder, runs okf's script with `{}` on stdin, and prints
56|okf's reason with `"decision": "continue"` when okf blocks. In every other
57|case, a missing script or a failure included, it prints `{}` and exits 0,
58|so it never breaks a turn (ADR 0004).
59|
60|After APM's install, kmctl takes every handler running `okf-stop-check.sh`
61|out of `.agents/hooks.json`, dropping a named hook left empty and keeping
62|the rest. `kmctl doctor` fails `antigravity.apm-hooks` while that file
63|still runs it, and `antigravity.hook` covers both of kmctl's hooks.
64|
65|Rejected:
66|
67|- Leaving APM's handler and only adding kmctl's. agy would still log the
68|  failed handler at every turn's end.
69|- Dropping okf's check for Antigravity. A bundle that opts in to
70|  `upkeep: enforced` would get it in Claude Code only.
71|
72|## Consequences
73|
74|- An Antigravity session in a repository with `upkeep: enforced` gets
75|  okf's reminder once per turn, as Claude Code does.
76|- The handler depends on okf's script path and its exact
77|  `"decision":"block"` output; a change to either in okf-skills makes the
78|  hook print `{}`, which is safe but silent.
79|- A bare `apm install` puts APM's handler back until the next
80|  `kmctl plugin install`, and doctor says so.
81|
82|### Amended, 2026-10-17
83|
84|[ADR 0020](0020-apm-installs-the-hooks-mcp-server-and-rules-kmctl-patches-the-rest.md):
85|kmctl's package now ships the SessionStart hooks, okf's MCP server and the
86|rules for each harness, and APM writes them; kmctl writes only the
87|Antigravity agents and removes APM's broken okf Stop handler.
[end of file]

15|# ADR 0019: kmctl plugin remove uninstalls the package and reinstalls the harnesses kept
16|
17|## Context
18|
19|The operator asked (2026-10-17) for `kmctl plugin remove`: a way to take
20|kmctl out of a repository without APM on PATH. An install leaves files from
21|two owners. APM writes kmctl's and okf's skills, agent, rules and okf's
22|hooks, and records them in `apm.lock.yaml`
23|([ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md)). kmctl writes the
24|SessionStart hook, the `okf-bundle` MCP entry and, for Antigravity,
25|`.agents/plugins/kmctl/` ([ADR 0015](0015-antigravity-gets-skills-and-rules-from-apm-and-a-kmctl-plugin-folder.md)).
26|
27|What APM 0.33.0 does, from the ticket's spikes:
28|
29|- `apm uninstall` on kmctl's entry removes both packages, their deployed
30|  files and hooks for every target, and the lock; it leaves `{}` in
31|  `.agents/hooks.json` (spike:plugin-remove/3).
32|- It takes the entry as `HOST[:PORT]/OWNER/REPO/apm`, the case of the
33|  entry's own `git:` URL; the lock lowercases a GitHub repo_url, so the name
34|  is built from the entry (spike:plugin-remove/5).
35|- Dropping one target from `targets:` and installing again leaves okf's
36|  Antigravity hook script behind, recorded in the lock as a `legacy`
37|  target (spike:plugin-remove/2).
38|- `kmctl plugin install` only adds targets, so `apm.yml` cannot say whether
39|  a target was there before kmctl.
40|
41|## Decision
42|
43|`kmctl plugin remove --harness LIST` uninstalls kmctl's entry with APM, then
44|removes what kmctl wrote for each harness named: the SessionStart hook and
45|the `okf-bundle` server for Claude Code (with `claude mcp remove` at user
46|scope), the plugin folder and an empty `.agents/hooks.json` for
47|Antigravity. When some installed harnesses are kept, it installs them again
48|with the normal install, from the removed entry's source at its `ref`, so
49|their version does not change. If that install fails it exits 1, says the
50|kept harnesses were uninstalled too, and names the install that puts them
51|back.
52|
53|A removed harness leaves `targets:` only when no other dependency is left
54|in `apm.yml`; otherwise the target stays, with a note, so the repository's
55|own packages keep it. `kmctl doctor` counts `targets:` only when the lock
56|lists no kmctl package, so a kept target does not mark a removed harness as
57|installed. Without `--harness`, remove asks at a terminal, as install does
58|since the harness question, with the installed harnesses as the default.
59|
60|Rejected:
61|
62|- Rewriting `targets:` and running `apm install` for the rest. It leaves
63|  okf's Antigravity hook script behind (spike:plugin-remove/2).
64|- Deleting APM's files by hand from the lock's list. APM's own uninstall
65|  does it and keeps the lock consistent.
66|- Dropping a removed harness from `targets:` always. It would stop the
67|  repository's other packages deploying to that harness.
68|
69|## Consequences
70|
71|- Removing one of two harnesses reinstalls the other, so it needs the
72|  network and the source's tag, as an install does.
73|- After a partial remove, a bare `apm install` without `--target` can
74|  deploy kmctl to a harness whose target was kept; remove says so.
75|- `kmctl plugin remove` with nothing installed changes nothing and exits 0.
76|
77|## Correction, 2026-10-17
78|
79|Superseded by [ADR 0021](0021-apm-installs-kmctl-s-package-kmctl-plugin-patch-adds-the-rest.md).

19|# ADR 0020: APM installs the hooks, MCP server and rules; kmctl patches the rest
20|
21|## Context
22|
23|Since [ADR 0014](0014-apm-is-the-only-install-route.md) kmctl wrote some of
24|its install itself: the Claude Code SessionStart hook and okf's MCP server,
25|and for Antigravity a plugin folder holding the agents, the rules
26|([ADR 0016](0016-antigravity-rules-come-from-the-kmctl-plugin-folder.md)),
27|the hooks and the MCP server
28|([ADR 0015](0015-antigravity-gets-skills-and-rules-from-apm-and-a-kmctl-plugin-folder.md),
29|[ADR 0018](0018-kmctl-runs-okf-s-stop-check-for-antigravity.md)). Each came
30|from a narrow spike that APM did not do it, not from APM's documentation as
31|a whole. The operator asked (2026-10-17) to hand back to APM everything APM
32|can do and to document what it cannot.
33|
34|A review of apm-cli 0.33.0's source (the newest release) and the ticket's
35|spikes found:
36|
37|- A package can ship hooks (`.apm/hooks/hooks.json`); APM merges them into
38|  `.claude/settings.json` and `.agents/hooks.json`, records what it wrote in
39|  `apm-hooks.json`, and keeps every command byte for byte
40|  (spike:apm-hands-back/3).
41|- A package can declare an MCP server under `dependencies.mcp`. APM trusts a
42|  direct dependency's server and writes it to `.mcp.json`,
43|  `.agents/mcp_config.json` and, with `-g`, the user `.claude.json`; it skips
44|  a transitive one, which is why kmctl's package declares okf's server
45|  itself (spike:apm-hands-back/1, /5).
46|- A package can depend on sub-packages by relative path, each with its own
47|  `targets:`, so each harness gets only its own rules and hooks
48|  (spike:apm-hands-back/1). APM resolves every sub-package whatever the
49|  target, so each needs an `.apm/` folder (spike:apm-hands-back/4).
50|- agy loads a SessionStart hook from the workspace `.agents/hooks.json` under
51|  APM's hook name `apm`, and okf's server from `.agents/mcp_config.json`
52|  (spike:apm-hands-back/2).
53|- APM writes an Antigravity rule's several globs as a YAML list, which agy
54|  refuses; written in `applyTo` as `**/` globs joined by escaped commas
55|  (`\,`), they come out as the one string agy reads
56|  (spike:apm-hands-back/1). The `\,` escape is meant for a comma inside one
57|  glob, so this leans on APM's parser.
58|
59|## Decision
60|
61|kmctl's package is three APM packages in `apm/`:
62|
63|- `apm/` (shared): the skills, kmctl-auditor, the okf-skills dependency,
64|  okf's MCP server `okf-bundle` under `dependencies.mcp` (kmctl's `sh`
65|  launcher at the pinned okf commit), and `./claude` and `./antigravity`.
66|- `apm/claude/` (`targets: [claude]`): the four rules, and the SessionStart
67|  hook running `kmctl briefing`.
68|- `apm/antigravity/` (`targets: [antigravity]`): the four rules, generated
69|  from the Claude copies by `scripts/sync_antigravity_rules.py` (a test fails
70|  when a copy is stale; each copy opens with an HTML comment naming its
71|  source, the script and this decision); the SessionStart hook running
72|  `kmctl briefing --format antigravity`; and ADR 0018's okf Stop wrapper,
73|  now running from `.agents/`.
74|
75|`kmctl plugin install` writes none of these. It removes, before running APM,
76|what an older kmctl wrote that APM now writes, at project and user scope: a
77|kmctl SessionStart group APM's `apm-hooks.json` does not record, and an
78|`okf-bundle` entry that differs from the package's. `kmctl doctor` checks the
79|files APM writes.
80|
81|What APM cannot do yet, and what kmctl does meanwhile:
82|
83|| Gap | Stopgap | Drop it when |
84||---|---|---|
85|| APM writes no agents for Antigravity (APM issue #2990, accepted, unreleased; it will not translate tool names either). | kmctl writes `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` with `plugin.json` and the agents translated from Claude Code's format. | APM ships agents for Antigravity and kmctl's package can ship an Antigravity-format agent file in `apm/antigravity/`. |
86|| APM writes okf's Antigravity Stop hook as `bash ".agents/hooks/okf-skills/hooks/okf-stop-check.sh"`, a path from the repository root, but agy runs hooks in `.agents/`; okf also prints Claude Code's `"block"`. No APM issue is filed. | kmctl takes that handler out of `.agents/hooks.json`; the package's wrapper runs okf's check instead (ADR 0018). | APM writes Antigravity hook paths relative to `.agents/`, or okf ships target-specific hook files with agy's output. |
87|| `apm uninstall -g` leaves `okf-bundle` in the user `.claude.json` (spike:apm-hands-back/5); at project scope uninstall removes it. | None; the install how-to gives `claude mcp remove okf-bundle --scope user`. | APM removes a user-scope MCP server on uninstall. |
88|| A consumer whose `apm.yml` limits executables (an `executables:` block, or the deprecated `allowExecutables:`) gets no hook or MCP server from a package it has not approved. | None; the docs say to run `apm approve --pending` and approve kmctl's package. | Not an APM bug: the consumer's choice. |
89|| A user with their own okf server under another name now gets `okf-bundle` as well; kmctl used to add none then. | None; the README warns to uninstall the okf plugin (`okf@scaccogatto`), and doctor passes either way. | APM can skip a server another entry already provides. |
90|
91|Rejected:
92|
93|- Keeping kmctl's own writers. Two owners of the same hook and server meant
94|  two copies of each after an `apm install`, and state APM did not record.
95|- One Antigravity rule file per glob, which works without the escape. It
96|  turns four rules into a dozen files and splits each rule's guidance.
97|
98|## Consequences
99|
100|- `apm install` (or `apm update`) alone keeps the hook, rules and MCP
101|  server current; `apm uninstall` removes them.
102|- kmctl's remaining install-time work is the two stopgaps above; the next
103|  ticket moves it to `kmctl plugin patch`.
104|- ADR 0016 is superseded: the rules come from APM again, in the form agy
105|  reads. ADRs 0014, 0015 and 0018 point here for what changed.
106|
107|Supersedes [ADR 0016](0016-antigravity-rules-come-from-the-kmctl-plugin-folder.md).
[end of file]

15|
16|# ADR 0021: APM installs kmctl's package; kmctl plugin patch adds the rest
17|
18|## Context
19|
20|After [ADR 0020](0020-apm-installs-the-hooks-mcp-server-and-rules-kmctl-patches-the-rest.md)
21|APM installs everything in kmctl's package: the skills, rules, SessionStart
22|hooks and okf's MCP server. `kmctl plugin install` and `update` still wrote
23|the `apm.yml` entry and ran APM for the user, and `kmctl plugin remove`
24|([ADR 0019](0019-kmctl-plugin-remove-uninstalls-the-package-and-reinstalls-the-harnesses-kept.md))
25|ran `apm uninstall` and installed the kept harnesses again. That wrapper
26|made kmctl a second front end for APM's own verbs. The operator asked
27|(2026-10-17) for one command, `kmctl plugin patch`, that replaces install
28|and update, with installing, upgrading and removing left to APM, and for
29|the install instructions per harness in the README.
30|
31|## Decision
32|
33|APM installs, upgrades and removes kmctl's package: the user adds
34|`{git: https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management.git, path: apm,
35|ref: vVERSION}` to `apm.yml` (the version of the kmctl CLI they run) and
36|runs `apm install` (`-g` for Claude Code at user scope), `apm update`, or
37|`apm uninstall`.
38|
39|`kmctl plugin patch [--scope project|user] [--json] [--undo]`, run after
40|`apm install`, adds what APM cannot install yet (ADR 0020's table). It
41|never runs APM and needs neither uv nor APM on PATH. It reads
42|`apm.lock.yaml` to see which harnesses APM installed kmctl's package for,
43|then, for Antigravity, writes `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` (the translated
44|agents) and takes APM's broken okf Stop handler out of `.agents/hooks.json`;
45|for Claude Code, it removes what an older kmctl wrote that APM now writes
46|(saying to run `apm install` again when APM must write it) and the old
47|claude plugin `kmctl@kmctl`. It refuses, naming the fix, when the lock lists
48|no kmctl package, and before that when `apm.yml` still names the package as
49|kmctl v0.3.0 and older did, naming the `apm uninstall` to run first.
50|`--undo` deletes `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` and nothing else.
51|
52|`kmctl plugin install`, `update` and `remove`, and the harness question,
53|leave the CLI. doctor's fixes name `apm install`, the `apm.yml` ref or
54|`kmctl plugin patch`. The README's install section gives the steps for
55|Claude Code, Antigravity and both.
56|
57|Rejected:
58|
59|- Keeping `install` as a wrapper. It duplicated APM's verbs and kept kmctl
60|  in the business of writing `apm.yml`.
61|- Making `patch` run `apm install` itself. The user then needs APM through
62|  uv for kmctl to work; patch would stop being the small, offline step it is.
63|
64|## Consequences
65|
66|- Users need APM (`uvx --from apm-cli==0.33.0 apm` works without installing
67|  it) and keep the `apm.yml` ref equal to their kmctl version themselves;
68|  doctor's `claude.lock` and `antigravity.lock` say when they differ.
69|- `kmctl plugin patch` has to run after every `apm install` or `apm update`
70|  for Antigravity, since APM rewrites `.agents/hooks.json`.
71|- ADR 0019 is superseded; ADR 0014 points here for the route.
72|
73|Supersedes [ADR 0019](0019-kmctl-plugin-remove-uninstalls-the-package-and-reinstalls-the-harnesses-kept.md).
[end of file]

# kmctl's APM package (ADR 0014, ADR 0020). A repository's apm.yml names it as
# {git: https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management.git, path: apm, ref: vVERSION}
# and apm install brings, for every harness, the skills, the audit agent (Claude
# Code only: APM writes no agents for Antigravity) and the okf skills, plus
# okf's MCP server below; ./claude and ./antigravity add each harness's rules
# and hooks. The version below is the one release version (ADR 0012):
# scripts/release.py set writes it into every kmctl apm.yml, and pyproject.toml
# reads it.
name: kmctl
version: 0.3.0
description: kmctl's skills, audit agent, knowledge rules and session hooks, with the okf skills and MCP server they use.
dependencies:
  apm:
    - scaccogatto/okf-skills#a8b96420de90d102c43cda1693d01ec4f925f2ab
    - ./claude
    - ./antigravity
  mcp:
    # okf's MCP server, declared here because APM skips a transitive
    # dependency's server; the launcher runs okf_mcp.py at the okf-skills
    # commit above for the nearest .okf/ (kmctl.plugin.okf_mcp_launcher).
    - name: okf-bundle
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: sh
      args:
        - "-c"
        - "for d in \"$PWD\"; do [ -n \"$d\" ] || continue; d=$(cd \"$d\" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || continue; while :; do if [ -d \"$d/.okf\" ]; then exec uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills/a8b96420de90d102c43cda1693d01ec4f925f2ab/servers/okf_mcp.py \"$d/.okf\"; fi; [ \"$d\" = / ] && break; d=$(dirname \"$d\"); done; done; exec uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills/a8b96420de90d102c43cda1693d01ec4f925f2ab/servers/okf_mcp.py .okf"

177|def _cause(output: str) -> str:
178|    """The lines of ``output`` that say why a tool failed, joined with "; ".
179|
180|    git's ``fatal:`` and ``error:`` lines and APM's ``[x]`` lines name the
181|    cause, but the tool may print them before a last line that does not. So
182|    keep those lines in order, then the last line, cut to CAUSE_CAP
183|    characters.
184|    """
185|    lines = [line.strip() for line in output.strip().splitlines() if line.strip()]
186|    if not lines:
187|        return "no output"
188|    kept = [line for line in lines if line.startswith(("fatal:", "error:", "[x]"))]
189|    if lines[-1] not in kept[-1:]:
190|        kept.append(lines[-1])
191|    cause = "; ".join(kept)
192|    return cause if len(cause) <= CAUSE_CAP else cause[: CAUSE_CAP - 1] + "…"

229|    list[str]

465|def okf_mcp_launcher(starts: Sequence[str] = ('"$PWD"',)) -> str:
466|    """A POSIX sh script that starts okf's MCP server on the nearest ``.okf/`` folder.
467|
468|    It walks up from each start folder in turn to the first folder holding
469|    ``.okf/`` and runs ``uv run <okf_mcp_url()> <that folder>/.okf``. When no
470|    start leads to one, it passes ``.okf``, so the server starts and its tools
471|    report that there is no bundle instead of the server failing to start.
472|
473|    Parameters
474|    ----------
475|    starts :
476|        Shell words naming the folders to start from, tried in order; one
477|        that is empty or not a folder is skipped. The default is the working
478|        folder. The Antigravity plugin passes its own folder first.
479|    """
480|    url = okf_mcp_url()
481|    return (
482|        f"for d in {' '.join(starts)}; do "
483|        '[ -n "$d" ] || continue; '
484|        'd=$(cd "$d" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || continue; '
485|        "while :; do "
486|        f'if [ -d "$d/.okf" ]; then exec uv run {url} "$d/.okf"; fi; '
487|        '[ "$d" = / ] && break; d=$(dirname "$d"); '
488|        "done; done; "
489|        f"exec uv run {url} .okf"
490|    )

534|def drop_old_hook(settings: Path) -> bool:
535|    """Take out the SessionStart hooks an older kmctl wrote into ``settings``; return whether any went.
536|
537|    Since ADR 0020 APM writes kmctl's hook from the package and records each
538|    group it wrote in ``apm-hooks.json``. A group that runs ``kmctl briefing``
539|    and is not recorded there holds kmctl's own hook, from before; left in
540|    place, the briefing would print twice (spike:apm-hands-back/3, /5). Only
541|    kmctl's hooks leave such a group, which goes when nothing else is left in
542|    it. Every other key, group and hook stays; a missing file is left missing.
543|    """
544|    if not settings.is_file():
545|        return False
546|    data = read_json(settings)
547|    hooks = data.get("hooks")
548|    groups = hooks.get("SessionStart") if isinstance(hooks, dict) else None
549|    if not isinstance(groups, list):
550|        return False
551|    recorded = _apm_recorded_groups(settings)
552|    kept: list[object] = []
553|    dropped = False
554|    for group in groups:

556|        ours = isinstance(inner, list) and any(_is_kmctl_hook(h) for h in inner)

568|    if not dropped:

570|    assert isinstance(hooks, dict)
571|    if kept:
572|        hooks["SessionStart"] = kept
573|    else:

174|def package_hooks(harness: str) -> dict[str, object]:

200|def _apm_hooks_data(cwd: Path) -> dict[str, object] | None:
201|    """APM's hooks.json in ``cwd``, parsed; None when the file is missing.
202|
203|    Raises
204|    ------
205|    PluginError
206|        When the file is not a JSON object.

208|    path = cwd / APM_HOOKS
209|    if not path.is_file():

212|        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
213|    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):

216|        raise PluginError(f"{APM_HOOKS.as_posix()} is not a JSON object")

221|    """Whether any handler in a parsed hooks.json runs okf's Stop check script."""
222|    return any(
223|        _runs_okf_stop(handler)
224|        for events in data.values()
225|        if isinstance(events, dict)
226|        for handlers in events.values()

232|def apm_okf_stop_present(cwd: Path) -> bool:
233|    """Whether APM's hooks.json in ``cwd`` still runs okf's Stop check, which never works there.
234|

236|    command runs the script counts.

238|    Raises
239|    ------

242|        agy cannot load either.

248|def drop_apm_okf_stop(cwd: Path) -> bool:
249|    """Take okf's Stop handlers out of APM's hooks.json in ``cwd``; return whether any went.
250|
251|    APM writes okf's handler with a path from the repository root, but agy
252|    runs it in ``.agents/``, so it fails at the end of every turn; the
253|    package's Stop wrapper, which names the script too, stays and runs it
254|    instead. A named hook
255|    left with no handlers is dropped; every other hook and key stays. A
256|    file that is missing or not a JSON object is left alone.
257|    """
258|    path = cwd / APM_HOOKS
259|    try:
260|        data = _apm_hooks_data(cwd)
261|    except PluginError:
262|        return False
263|    if data is None:
264|        return False
265|    changed = False
266|    for name, events in list(data.items()):
267|        if not isinstance(events, dict):
268|            continue
269|        dropped = False
270|        for event, handlers in list(events.items()):
271|            if not isinstance(handlers, list):
272|                continue
273|            kept = [h for h in handlers if not _runs_okf_stop(h)]
274|            if len(kept) != len(handlers):
275|                dropped = True
276|                if kept:
277|                    events[event] = kept
278|                else:
279|                    del events[event]
280|        if dropped and not events:
281|            del data[name]
282|        changed = changed or dropped
283|    if changed:
284|        path.write_text(_json(data), encoding="utf-8")
285|    return changed

329|    for rel, text in want.items():

337|    """How ``folder`` differs from ``want``: (path inside it, ``missing``, ``differs`` or ``extra``), sorted."""
338|    have = {

340|        for p in folder.rglob("*")
341|        if p.is_file() or p.is_symlink()
342|    }
343|    found = []

1|# Cut a release by hand (ADR 0012). Pick an increment or type the version; a
2|# dry run (the default) resolves, tests and builds, then stops. A real run from
3|# main opens a pull request that sets both apm.yml files (apm/apm.yml is the
4|# one version source) to the version and pins the docs' install lines to its
5|# tag; merging it is the approval, and release-tag.yml tags the merge commit
6|# and publishes the GitHub Release.
7|# Releases go to GitHub only, never to PyPI.
8|name: Release
9|
10|on:
11|  workflow_dispatch:
12|    inputs:
13|      increment:
14|        description: "Raise the newest v* tag: PATCH, MINOR, MAJOR, PRE (next pre-release), FINAL (promote a pre-release). Ignored when version is set."
15|        type: choice
16|        required: true
17|        default: PATCH
18|        options: [PATCH, MINOR, MAJOR, PRE, FINAL]
19|      prerelease:
20|        description: "Start or switch a pre-release series: a, b or rc. none for a release."
21|        type: choice
22|        required: true
23|        default: none
24|        options: [none, a, b, rc]
25|      version:
26|        description: "Override: the exact version, X.Y.Z or X.Y.Z{a,b,rc}N, no v. Required for the first release."
27|        type: string
28|        required: false
29|      dry_run:
30|        description: "Resolve, test and build, then stop without opening the version pull request."
31|        type: boolean
32|        required: true
33|        default: true
34|
35|concurrency:
36|  group: release
37|  cancel-in-progress: false
38|
39|permissions:
40|  contents: read
41|
42|jobs:
43|  resolve:
44|    name: Resolve the version
45|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
46|    outputs:
47|      version: ${{ steps.next.outputs.version }}
48|    steps:
49|      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
50|        with:
51|          fetch-depth: 0
52|      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
53|        with:
54|          enable-cache: true
55|      - name: Work out the version
56|        id: next
57|        env:
58|          INCREMENT: ${{ inputs.increment }}
59|          PRE: ${{ inputs.prerelease }}
60|          OVERRIDE: ${{ inputs.version }}
61|        shell: bash
62|        run: |
63|          set -euo pipefail
64|          args=("$INCREMENT")
65|          if [ "$PRE" != "none" ]; then args+=(--pre "$PRE"); fi
66|          if [ -n "$OVERRIDE" ]; then args+=(--version "$OVERRIDE"); fi
67|          VERSION="$(uv run scripts/next_release_version.py "${args[@]}")"
68|          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

70|        if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run && github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
71|        run: |
72|          echo "::error::A release is cut only from main, not $GITHUB_REF. Run it from main, or keep dry run on."
73|          exit 1
74|      - name: Refuse a tag that exists on origin
75|        env:
76|          VERSION: ${{ steps.next.outputs.version }}
77|        shell: bash
78|        run: |
79|          set -euo pipefail
80|          set +e
81|          git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/v$VERSION" >/dev/null
82|          rc=$?
83|          set -e
84|          case "$rc" in
85|            2) ;;
86|            0) echo "::error::Tag v$VERSION already exists. Pick the next version."; exit 1 ;;
87|            *) echo "::error::Could not check whether v$VERSION exists (git exit $rc)."; exit 1 ;;
88|          esac
89|      - name: Summary
90|        env:
91|          VERSION: ${{ steps.next.outputs.version }}
92|          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
93|        run: |
94|          {
95|            echo "## v$VERSION"
96|            echo
97|            echo "| | |"
98|            echo "|---|---|"
99|            echo "| commit | \`$GITHUB_SHA\` |"
100|            echo "| dry run | $DRY_RUN |"
101|          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

111|      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0

1|# Tag and publish a release when its version pull request lands on main
2|# (ADR 0012). Only a push that raises apm/apm.yml's version to a
3|# releasable version releases; an unchanged or .dev version does nothing, a
4|# lowered one fails, and a push with no previous commit to compare against (the
5|# repository's first push) is skipped. The wheel and sdist are built and checked
6|# before the tag exists, so a failed build leaves no tag behind; a rerun after a
7|# failed publish resumes from the tag it pushed. The GitHub Release carries the
8|# wheel, the sdist and their checksums; nothing goes to PyPI.
9|#
10|# No concurrency group: a group keeps one pending run and cancels the rest,
11|# which would drop the tag of a version merged between two others.
12|name: Release tag
13|
14|on:
15|  push:
16|    branches: [main]
17|    paths:
18|      - apm/apm.yml
19|
20|permissions:
21|  contents: read

24|  tag:
25|    name: Tag and publish the release
26|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
27|    permissions:
28|      contents: write
29|    steps:
30|      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
31|        with:
32|          fetch-depth: 0
33|      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
34|        with:
35|          enable-cache: true

37|      # or nothing. A tag at another commit fails.
38|      - name: Decide whether this push releases
39|        id: plan
40|        env:
41|          BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
42|          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
43|        shell: bash
44|        run: |
45|          set -euo pipefail
46|          VERSION="$(uv run scripts/release.py current)"

48|          if [ -z "$BEFORE" ] || [ "$BEFORE" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] \

5|"""The release workflows' helper: read, set and compare the release version (ADR 0012).
6|
7|Usage::
8|
9|    uv run scripts/release.py current
10|    uv run scripts/release.py set VERSION
11|    uv run scripts/release.py compare OLD NEW
12|    uv run scripts/release.py is-prerelease VERSION
13|
14|``apm/apm.yml``, kmctl's APM package, carries the one version, and
15|``pyproject.toml`` reads it from there (ADR 0014). APM needs a ``version:`` in
16|each apm.yml, so ``set`` writes it and copies it into the root ``apm.yml``;
17|``current`` refuses when the copy differs. ``set`` also points the six install lines in the docs, and the
18|APM how-to's package pins and CLI install line, at the tag ``vVERSION``. This script never
19|commits or tags: ``.github/workflows/release.yml`` opens the version pull
20|request and ``release-tag.yml`` tags the merge, so there is one release path.
21|"""
22|
23|from __future__ import annotations
24|
25|import argparse
26|import re
27|import sys
28|from pathlib import Path
29|
30|from packaging.version import InvalidVersion, Version

32|#: The one version source, which pyproject.toml's [tool.hatch.version] reads.
33|MANIFEST = Path("apm/apm.yml")
34|#: The docs whose install lines ``set`` points at the release tag.
35|DOC_FILES = (
36|    Path("README.md"),
37|    Path("docs/tutorials/get-started-with-kmctl.md"),
38|    Path("docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md"),

43|#: package and its two per-harness sub-packages (ADR 0020).
44|APM_FILES = (
45|    Path("apm.yml"),
46|    MANIFEST,
47|    Path("apm/claude/apm.yml"),
48|    Path("apm/antigravity/apm.yml"),
49|)

# /continue: pick the work back up

Handoffs are concepts in `.okf/handoffs/`, written by `/handoff`. This skill
lists the live ones, lets the user choose, and briefs them on the chosen work.
It reads only; it changes nothing until the user says what to do.

## 1. List the live handoffs

```
kmctl handoffs --json
```

It prints the live handoffs newest first, each with `id`, `path`, `title`,
`description` and `date`. Expired ones are left out. If `$ARGUMENTS` names a
topic, keep the ones whose title or description match it, and fall back to
the full list when none do. If the list is empty, say there are no live
handoffs, suggest `/handoff` at the end of the next session, and stop.

## 2. Let the user choose

Ask with AskUserQuestion, `multiSelect: true`, so they can pick several. A
question holds at most four options, so offer the three newest handoffs plus a
fourth option, `more`:

- `label`: a number and the handoff's title;
- `description`: its description and date.

If they pick `more`, ask again with the next three. If they pick nothing, ask
once more, then stop. Never pick for them. When you cannot ask (no
AskUserQuestion), show the same choice as text: the three newest as numbered
lines plus "more", and stop for their reply. If the user already named the
handoffs they want in their message, skip the question and go to step 3.

## 3. Load and sum up

Read the chosen handoffs at their `path`. Give one combined brief: what each
piece of work is, where it stands, threads that connect or conflict, and the
open next steps. Name the handoffs by title so the user knows what fed it.

## 4. Ask what to do next

End with the question: continue one of these threads, start something new, or
refine the summary? Take no action before the answer.

# /handoff: write where the work stands

A handoff is a short technical brief for someone picking the work up cold: what
it is, what was decided and why, where it stands, and what comes next. It is a
concept in `.okf/handoffs/`, so it travels with the repository and `/continue`
can find it. It expires after two weeks (`kmctl review due` lists it then).

## 1. Reconstruct the work

Read back over the conversation, and `$ARGUMENTS` if the user named a focus.
Capture the substance: the goal, the approach, the decisions and their reasons,
what is done, what is half done or untested, and the open questions. Name real
files, branches, commands and tickets; vague summaries save nobody any work.

## 2. Save it with kmctl

```
kmctl new handoff 'Short title of the work' --description 'One sentence: what and where it stands.' ${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:+--key "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"} --json
```

The key ties the handoff to this Claude Code session, so a second `/handoff`
in the same session updates the same handoff instead of adding another. Pass
`--key` only when `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is set and not empty (the
`${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:+...}` form above does this); kmctl refuses an empty
key. kmctl writes the front matter, the index entry and the log
line, and prints the path. If it refuses because `.okf/` is missing, say so and
suggest `kmctl init`; do not write the file yourself.

## 3. Write the four sections

Fill in the sections kmctl wrote at that path, in prose a capable colleague can
act on:

- **Summary**: what the work is, the approach, and the key decisions with why.
- **Where it stands**: done and working; in progress; untested or uncertain.
- **Next steps**: the concrete threads to pick up, specific enough to start on.
- **Key references**: files, branches, PRs, tickets, commands, links.

## 4. Confirm

Run `kmctl check`, then tell the user the handoff's title and path in one line,
and that `/continue` will offer it in a later session.

Use when someone asks to audit, review or check the knowledge bundle, the decision log, the architecture docs or the practices, asks "is our documentation still true", or runs /audit, optionally naming one kind ("audit the architecture docs").
---

# /audit: check knowledge against reality, report only

The audit reads; it never edits `.okf/` or `docs/`, and it writes no
`verified` entry (ADR 0005). The person reading the report decides what to fix.

## 1. Get what is due

```
kmctl review due --json
```

Keep the entries in `due` whose id starts with `architecture/`, `decisions/` or
`practices/`. Other kinds (the manifesto, proposals, prototypes, handoffs) are
not audited here; mention how many you left out. If the user named one kind,
keep only that kind. If the user named concepts, use those whether or not
they are due. If nothing is left, say nothing in scope is due and stop.

## 2. Batch by kind

Group the concepts by kind and split each group into batches of at most ten,
so each run reads a manageable amount.

## 3. Hand each batch to the auditor

Read the review skill for the batch's kind, next to this skill in the plugin:
`../architecture-review/SKILL.md`, `../decision-log-review/SKILL.md` or
`../practices-review/SKILL.md`. Dispatch the `kmctl-auditor` agent with the
repository root, the batch (id, path and reasons from step 1) and that review
skill's text. The agent has only Read, Grep and Glob, so it cannot change
anything. Run batches in parallel when there are several.

## 4. Report

Collect the agents' JSON blocks. Show a table per kind with each concept, its
verdict and its one-line summary, `drifted` first, then `unsure`, then
`holds`, followed by the evidence for anything drifted. End with the counts and
the combined JSON block, so a script or the CI action can read it. Do not fix
anything or offer edits unless the user asks.

13|  percent-decoded, as GitHub renders it. Reference-style definitions

1|"""Supersede one decision record with another, writing both sides of the link.
2|
3|A record is never rewritten: the old one gets ``status: deprecated`` and an
4|appended dated Correction section, and its body above that stays as it was
5|(``.claude/rules/okf-bundle.md``). Only spec fields are written (I4); any
6|other key a person added to the front matter is left alone.
7|"""
8|
9|import re
10|from dataclasses import dataclass
11|from datetime import UTC, datetime
12|from pathlib import Path
13|
14|from kmctl.concepts import ConceptError, append_log
15|from kmctl.kinds import CORRECTION, DEPRECATED
16|from kmctl.okf import BadFrontMatter, field, front_matter
17|
18|
19|@dataclass(frozen=True)
20|class Superseded:
21|    """The two records ``supersede`` linked, as concept ids."""
22|
23|    old: str
24|    new: str
25|
26|
27|def _number(value: str) -> str:
28|    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value):
29|        raise ConceptError(f"{value!r} is not a decision number; give it as 3 or 0003")
30|    return f"{int(value):04d}"
31|

33|def _record(decisions: Path, number: str) -> Path:
34|    found = sorted(decisions.glob(f"{number}-*.md"))
35|    if not found:
36|        raise ConceptError(
37|            f"no decision {number} in {decisions}; kmctl new decision creates one"
38|        )
39|    return found[0]
40|

42|def _entry_end(lines: list[str], start: int) -> int:
43|    """The last line of the entry starting at ``start``: it runs to a blank line or the next item."""
44|    end = start
45|    for i in range(start + 1, len(lines)):
46|        if not lines[i].strip() or re.match(r"^\s*[-*+]\s", lines[i]):
47|            break
48|        end = i
49|    return end
50|
51|
52|def _deprecate(text: str) -> str:
53|    """``text`` with its front matter ``status`` set to deprecated, body untouched."""
54|    end = text.index("\n---", 4)
55|    head, body = text[:end], text[end:]
56|    if re.search(r"^status:.*$", head, re.MULTILINE):
57|        head = re.sub(
58|            r"^status:.*$", f"status: {DEPRECATED}", head, count=1, flags=re.MULTILINE
59|        )
60|    else:
61|        head += f"\nstatus: {DEPRECATED}"
62|    return head + body
63|
64|
65|def supersede(
66|    root: Path, old: str, new: str, now: datetime | None = None
67|) -> Superseded:
68|    """Mark decision ``old`` superseded by decision ``new`` and link them both ways.
69|
70|    Parameters
71|    ----------
72|    root : Path
73|        The repository root, holding .okf/decisions/.
74|    old : str
75|        The number of the decision being replaced, such as ``3`` or ``0003``.
76|    new : str
77|        The number of the decision that replaces it.
78|    now : datetime | None
79|        The date written into the correction and the log; now when omitted.
80|
81|    Returns
82|    -------
83|    Superseded
84|        The ids of both records.
85|
86|    Raises
87|    ------
88|    ConceptError
89|        When either record is missing, they are the same, or ``old`` is
90|        already deprecated. Nothing is written.
91|    """
92|    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
93|    okf = root / ".okf"
94|    decisions = okf / "decisions"
95|    old_n, new_n = _number(old), _number(new)
96|    if old_n == new_n:
97|        raise ConceptError(
98|            f"a decision cannot supersede itself ({old_n}); give the new record's number to --by"
99|        )
100|    old_path, new_path = _record(decisions, old_n), _record(decisions, new_n)
101|    try:
102|        if field(front_matter(old_path), "status") == DEPRECATED:
103|            raise ConceptError(
104|                f"decision {old_n} is already deprecated; supersede the record that replaced it"
105|            )
106|    except BadFrontMatter as error:
107|        raise ConceptError(f"{error}; fix its front matter first") from error
108|    index = decisions / "index.md"
109|    lines = index.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if index.is_file() else []
110|    hits = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if f"]({old_path.name})" in line]
111|    if not hits:
112|        raise ConceptError(
113|            f"{index} has no entry for {old_path.name}; add a line "
114|            f"'- [title]({old_path.name}): description' to it, then run this again"
115|        )
116|
117|    date = now.date().isoformat()
118|    old_text = _deprecate(old_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).rstrip("\n")
119|    old_path.write_text(
120|        old_text
121|        + f"\n\n## {CORRECTION}, {date}\n\nSuperseded by [ADR {new_n}]({new_path.name}).\n",
122|        encoding="utf-8",
123|    )
124|    new_text = new_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip("\n")
125|    new_path.write_text(
126|        new_text + f"\n\nSupersedes [ADR {old_n}]({old_path.name}).\n", encoding="utf-8"
127|    )
128|    lines[_entry_end(lines, hits[0])] += f" (superseded by ADR {new_n})"
129|    index.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
130|    old_id = f"decisions/{old_path.stem}"
131|    new_id = f"decisions/{new_path.stem}"
132|    append_log(okf / "log.md", f"- Superseded `{old_id}` with `{new_id}`.", now)
133|    return Superseded(old=old_id, new=new_id)

"""Write kmctl's Antigravity rules from its Claude Code rules (ADR 0020).

APM 0.33.0 writes an Antigravity rule's ``applyTo`` globs as a YAML list when
there are several, which agy refuses, and agy matches a glob holding a ``/``
against the file's absolute path, so a repository-relative glob never matches
(spike:antigravity-rules/3). Written as one string of ``**/`` globs joined by
escaped commas, ``applyTo`` comes out of APM as the single ``globs:`` string
agy reads (spike:apm-hands-back/1). This script writes those copies into
``apm/antigravity/.apm/instructions/`` from ``apm/claude/.apm/instructions/``,
the one source; ``--check`` exits 1, naming each stale file, when a copy
differs, which a test runs.

Usage: uv run python -m scripts.sync_antigravity_rules [--check]
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
#: The rules as written for Claude Code: the one source.
SOURCE = ROOT / "apm" / "claude" / ".apm" / "instructions"
#: The generated copies for Antigravity.
TARGET = ROOT / "apm" / "antigravity" / ".apm" / "instructions"
#: The prefix agy needs on a glob that holds a ``/``.
ANY_FOLDER = "**/"


def antigravity_rule(text: str, source: str) -> str:
    """The Antigravity copy of one Claude Code rule file: ``applyTo`` rewritten, a generated-file notice, then the body unchanged.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        When the file has no front matter or no ``applyTo`` string.
    """
    end = text.find("\n---\n", 4)
    if not text.startswith("---\n") or end == -1:
        raise ValueError(f"{source} has no front matter")
    meta = yaml.safe_load(text[4:end]) or {}
    apply_to = meta.get("applyTo") if isinstance(meta, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(apply_to, str) or not apply_to.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{source} has no applyTo string")
    globs = [g.strip() for g in apply_to.split(",") if g.strip()]
    globs = [g if g.startswith(ANY_FOLDER) else ANY_FOLDER + g for g in globs]
    joined = "\\, ".join(globs)
    return (
        f"---\napplyTo: '{joined}'\n---\n{notice(Path(source).name)}{text[end + 5 :]}"
    )


def notice(name: str) -> str:
    """The comment that opens each generated rule's body, naming its source and why it exists."""
    return (

# kmctl kmctl keeps a repository's knowledge current: `docs/` for people who use the project and an `.okf/` knowledge bundle for people and agents working on it. At the start of every Claude Code session its plugin gives the agent a briefing on where knowledge lives, what is due for review and the rules for writing it. Its GitHub Action checks indexes and links on every pull request at no model cost, and an opt-in audit agent reports knowledge that has drifted from the code without changing anything. ## Why Agents write code faster than anyone updates the documents around it. The design page stops matching the code, a decision quietly gets reversed, and the next agent works from the stale version. No hook can tell whether a page is still true; that takes judgment. So kmctl does two things instead: - **It puts the right knowledge in front of the agent** at the start of each session: where knowledge lives, how to write it, and what is due for review. - **It audits.** A separate agent checks, on request or in CI, that decisions still hold, architecture pages still match the code and practices still have their evidence. It reports; a person decides. ## Where knowledge lives | Kind | Where | Reader | |---|---|---| | Docs for people who use the project | `docs/`, sorted into `tutorials/`, `how-to/`, `reference/` and `explanation/` | users | | Decisions, architecture, practices, proposals, handoffs | `.okf/`, an OKF v0.2 bundle | people and agents working on the project | | Repeatable tasks | skills | agents | | Standing guidance | rules in `.claude/rules/` | agents | ## What you get - **The `kmctl` CLI** sets a repository up, creates new decisions, docs pages and other concepts with their index entries, checks that indexes and links agree, and lists what is due for review. - **An APM package** for Claude Code and Antigravity, which [APM](https://microsoft.github.io/apm) installs: an audit agent, a skill for writing `docs/` pages, `/handoff` and `/continue` to save and resume work between sessions, and the knowledge rules, plus one SessionStart hook that prints the briefing. `kmctl plugin patch` adds the few pieces APM cannot install yet. - **A GitHub Action** that runs `kmctl check` on every pull request for free, and an opt-in audit you run by hand or on a schedule. ## Install ``` uv tool install git+https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management@v0.3.0 ``` The kmctl repository is private for now, so this needs a GitHub account with access to it; uv clones it with your git credentials. Then install kmctl's package in a repository with APM (Agent Package Manager). You do not need to install APM: `uvx --from apm-cli==0.33.0 apm` runs it through uv. If you have APM on your PATH, write `apm` instead. APM needs a GitHub token with access to the kmctl repository; see [Install kmctl with APM](docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md#before-you-start). Add kmctl's entry to `apm.yml` in the repository root. A new `apm.yml` looks like this: ```yaml name: my-project version: 0.1.0 dependencies: apm: - git: https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management.git path: apm ref: vX.Y.Z ``` Set `ref` to `v` and your kmctl version (`kmctl --version` prints it), so the package matches the CLI. Commit `apm.yml` and `apm.lock.yaml`. APM installs the package's hooks and MCP server unless `apm.yml` limits which packages may run them, with an `executables:` block (or the older `allowExecutables:`). If yours does, `apm approve --pending` lists kmctl's package; approve it with `apm approve`. > **Warning: uninstall the okf plugin first.** kmctl's package brings okf's > skills and its MCP server, `okf-bundle`. """Create one docs/ page in its Diataxis folder, with a skeleton and its docs/README.md entry."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from kmctl.concepts import ConceptError, link_text, one_line, slug
from kmctl.kinds import skeleton

DocType = Literal["tutorial", "how-to", "reference", "explanation"]

FOLDERS: dict[str, str] = {
    "tutorial": "tutorials",
    "how-to": "how-to",
    "reference": "reference",
    "explanation": "explanation",
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NewDoc:
    """What ``new_doc`` wrote."""

    path: str
    created_folder: bool


def new_doc(root: Path, doc_type: DocType, title: str, description: str = "") -> NewDoc:
    """Write a docs/ page of ``doc_type`` and add it to docs/README.md.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : Path
        The repository root, holding docs/README.md from ``kmctl init``.
    doc_type : DocType
        The Diataxis type, which picks the folder and the skeleton.
    title : str
        The page title; its kebab-case form names the file.
    description : str
        An optional line for the index entry.

    Returns
    -------
    NewDoc
        The page's path from the repository root, and whether its folder was created.

    Raises
    ------
    ConceptError
        When docs/README.md is missing or the page already exists. Nothing is written.
    """
    title = one_line(title)
    index = root / "docs" / "README.md"
    if not index.is_file():
        raise ConceptError(f"{index} does not exist; run kmctl init first")
    folder = root / "docs" / FOLDERS[doc_type]
    page = folder / f"{slug(title)}.md"
    if page.exists():
        raise ConceptError(
            f"{page.relative_to(root)} already exists; pick another title"
        )
    created_folder = not folder.is_dir()
    folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    body = "\n\n".join(f"## {h}" for h in skeleton(doc_type))
    page.write_text(f"# {title}\n\n{body}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    rel = page.relative_to(root / "docs").as_posix()
    entry = f"- [{link_text(title)}]({rel})" + (
        f": {one_line(description)}" if description.strip() else ""
    )
    text = index.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    index.write_text(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n" + entry + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return NewDoc(path=page.relative_to(root).as_posix(), created_folder=created_folder)

"""Work out the next release version from the newest ``v*`` tag (ADR 0012).

Usage::

    uv run scripts/next_release_version.py INCREMENT [--pre a|b|rc] [--version X] [--repo PATH]

INCREMENT is one of PATCH, MINOR, MAJOR (raise that part of the newest
release, optionally starting a pre-release series with ``--pre``), PRE (the
next pre-release of the same version: the counter, or a later label given
with ``--pre``) or FINAL (promote the newest pre-release to its release).
``--version`` overrides the arithmetic and is required for the first release,
when no tag exists. The version is printed without the ``v``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from collections.abc import Iterable
from pathlib import Path

from packaging.version import InvalidVersion, Version

INCREMENTS = ("PATCH", "MINOR", "MAJOR", "PRE", "FINAL")
PRE_LABELS = ("a", "b", "rc")


class Refused(Exception):
    """The version cannot be worked out; the message names the fix."""


def _parse(text: str) -> Version:
    """Parse a release version, refusing anything that is not one."""
    try:
        version = Version(text)
    except InvalidVersion as exc:
        raise Refused(
            f"{text!r} is not a version; type it like 0.2.0 or 0.2.0a1"
        ) from exc
    # One spelling per version, so the tag, the wheel and the manifest all agree.
    if str(version) != text:
        raise Refused(
            f"{text!r} is not written the canonical way; type it as {version}"
        )
    if len(version.release) != 3:
        raise Refused(f"{text!r} must name X.Y.Z, e.g. 0.2.0 or 0.2.0a1")
    return version


def newest_tag(tags: Iterable[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the highest version among ``v<version>`` tags, without the ``v``."""
    found: list[Version] = []
    for tag in tags:
        if not tag.startswith("v"):

"""The rules in .claude/rules/ that apm.yml does not install hold for kmctl.

The copied rules came from loop-harness. These tests fail when one still names
loop-harness, cites an ADR kmctl does not have, or points at a path that is
neither here nor planned.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RULES = ROOT / ".claude" / "rules"

#: Folders and files the design or a registered ticket says will exist.
PLANNED = (
    ".okf/architecture/",
    ".okf/practices/",
    ".okf/proposals/",
    ".okf/prototypes/",
    ".okf/handoffs/",
    "docs/",
    "src/kmctl/",
    ".github/workflows/",
    "action.yml",
)


def _apm_managed() -> set[str]:
    """Installed names of the rules apm.yml lists: `<name>.instructions.md` lands as `<name>.md`."""
    manifest = yaml.safe_load((ROOT / "apm.yml").read_text())
    entries = (e.partition("#")[0] for e in manifest["dependencies"]["apm"])
    suffix = ".instructions.md"
    return {
        Path(e).name.removesuffix(suffix) + ".md" for e in entries if e.endswith(suffix)
    }


def _own_rules() -> list[Path]:
    managed = _apm_managed()
    return sorted(p for p in RULES.glob("*.md") if p.name not in managed)


def _cited_paths(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Backticked tokens and paths: globs that look like repository paths."""
    tokens = re.findall(r"`([^`\s]+)`", text)
    match = re.search(r"^paths:\s*\[(.*)\]", text, re.MULTILINE)
    if match:
        tokens += re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', match.group(1))
    return [t for t in tokens if "/" in t and _from_root(t)]


def _from_root(token: str) -> bool:
    """True for a path from the repository root, not a slash command or a producer id."""
    first = token.split("/", 1)[0]
    roots = (
        {p.name for p in ROOT.iterdir()}
        | {p.split("/", 1)[0] for p in PLANNED}

def test_reference_covers_commands() -> None:
    text = _reference()
    commands = _commands(get_command(app))

        opt

def _depicts(text: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r"^## Depicts\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)

# kmctl knowledge bundle

For agents and people working on this repository. How to read and extend
this bundle is `.claude/rules/okf-bundle.md`.

12 concepts: the manifesto and 2 sections.

- [Manifesto](manifesto.md): what kmctl is for, where knowledge lives, the

  rejected.

  connect, as a diagram.
